a balcony slab must be supported (column.rule: A balcony slab must be supported (columns or cantilever) and reached by a door from its room; a floating slab with a railing but no support or access is a build error.

a downpipe must connect to a gutter at t.rule: A downpipe must connect to a gutter at the top and end in a splash block at the bottom; a bare cylinder is a placeholder, not a finished rain-water detail.

the main entrance must be legible: a cle.rule: The main entrance must be legible: a clear door leaf, handle, canopy or step detail, and an unambiguous porch/landing so a client can see where the front door is and how it is reached.

every from_documents window in a room mu.rule: Every from_documents window in a room must be visible in at least one of the room's required camera views; if no free camera point can show the room's key pieces and the window, the room layout must be changed, not the camera.

every from_documents door in a room must.rule: Every from_documents door in a room must be visible in at least one of the room's required camera views; if no free camera point can show the room's key pieces and the door, the room layout must be changed, not the camera.

a washbasin must be at a usable working.rule: A washbasin must be at a usable working height (rim ~0.85 m) and reachable; a basin wedged behind a toilet at a low height is a build error.

a bathroom door must not open directly i.rule: A bathroom door must not open directly into the basin/toilet cluster; the approach to the fixtures must be clear of the door swing.

a stair opening and landing edge must ha.rule: A stair opening and landing edge must have a proper guard (balustrade or full-height glass) with no large open gap; a thin placeholder glass panel is a fall risk and a build error.

the entrance area must have finished ste.rule: The entrance area must have finished steps, handrails, and a finished terrace slab; raw, untextured, floating geometry is a build error.

a door must be rendered as a door (leaf,.rule: A door must be rendered as a door (leaf, frame, handle), not as a different object (e.g. wall art); a door that looks like something else in a camera view is a build error.

a drawn piece must match its drawn size.rule: A drawn piece must match its drawn size and position within tolerance (0.05 m); a model that differs in size or place is a build error.

a drawn desk that the code retyped from.rule: A drawn desk that the code retyped from its size and room (adjusted_by_ai) is locked to that type; a 0.15 m offset from its drawn place is a fit error the furniture agent must resolve by re-fitting the piece, not by retyping it.

an interior camera that frames a door so.rule: An interior camera that frames a door so closely it reads as a wall panel must be moved to a free point that shows the door in context with the room's main furniture.

an interior camera in a hall that frames.rule: An interior camera in a hall that frames a door so closely it fills the frame must be moved to a free point that shows the door in context with the hall's other elements.

a drawn piece 0.21 x 0.20 m in a living.rule: A drawn piece 0.21 x 0.20 m in a living room that the AI could not type (potted_plant, unknown) and that is not built should be marked as not furniture if it is a symbol or mark, not a real piece.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side that is not built and has no type should be marked as not furniture if it is a group of symbols or marks, not real furniture.

a drawn piece 1.20 x 0.55 m in a bedroom.rule: A drawn piece 1.20 x 0.55 m in a bedroom that the documents name as a dresser ('*SIFONIYER') should be retyped as a dresser, not left untyped.

a dresser named by the documents at a lo.rule: A dresser named by the documents at a location where no drawn dresser stands should be added by the furniture agent if the nearest valid place is within 1.5 m of the text.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) that is.rule: A dressing room (Soyunma Odası) that is typed 'other' and holds only a wardrobe should be typed as a bedroom/dressing room and furnished as a set.

a small drawn piece around a level mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level mark text (e.g. '+0,50') that was read as furniture should be marked as a level mark, not furniture.

when the section prints the ground floor.rule: When the section prints the ground floor at a non-zero level (e.g. +0.50), the plans must be read with that offset so that all relative marks are correct.

a washing machine named by the documents.rule: A washing machine named by the documents in a bathroom should be verified by the furniture agent for correct placement and build status.

a dresser named by the documents in a be.rule: A dresser named by the documents in a bedroom should be verified by the furniture agent for correct placement and build status.
A dresser named by the documents in a bedroom that is not listed in the room's pieces should be added and placed by the furniture agent.

a 2.15 m sliding door read from its line.rule: A 2.15 m sliding door read from its lines (no swing arc) in the outer wall of a room, with a drawn piece standing across its approach, should be read as a window, not a door.

a 1.10 m gap in the outer wall of a room.rule: A 1.10 m gap in the outer wall of a room, with drawn pieces standing across its approach, should be read as a window, not a door.

an outer-wall gap that is fully or nearl.rule: An outer-wall gap that is fully or nearly blocked by a drawn fixed run (kitchen counter, bath wall) and has no outside access is a window at the floor's sill, not a door; the reading must classify it by what is on its approach, not by its width.

a bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toil.rule: A bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) must be solved as one unit so the pieces do not overlap; single-piece fixes that leave a real overlap are not a solution.

a dressing room's wardrobe and its partn.rule: A dressing room's wardrobe and its partners must be solved as one unit so the pieces do not overlap; single-piece fixes that leave a real overlap are not a solution.

a built piece must not cover a window op.rule: A built piece must not cover a window opening; the furniture agent must re-place the piece to clear the opening.

the big loop must run enough fix cycles.rule: The big loop must run enough fix cycles to raise the house score; stopping at the deadline with 303 open major points means the time budget was not used for more cycles.

a drawn piece whose type the room does n.rule: A drawn piece whose type the room does not allow must be retyped to a type that fits its size and its room, not kept unverified.

a dressing room smaller than the minimum.rule: A dressing room smaller than the minimum footprint of its dressing group (wardrobe + mirror + bench) must be flagged as too small for the group, and the group must be dropped or the room enlarged, not left with nothing placed.

a small drawn piece centred on a level-m.rule: A small drawn piece centred on a level-mark text (e.g. '+0,50') is a level-mark symbol, not furniture: mark it not_furniture with kind level_mark.

views flagged for review must be re-pose.rule: Views flagged for review must be re-posed or removed in the next agent round before the run is accepted.

when a tall storage piece (wardrobe) is.rule: When a tall storage piece (wardrobe) is drawn against a wall that also carries a window/door and no free wall span exists within the move limit, the fit stage must flag the drawing conflict for the architect (move the window or the piece) instead of letting the agent retry moves that the geometry forbids.

a kitchen room whose drawn run lacks a h.rule: A kitchen room whose drawn run lacks a hob/stove or a fridge must be completed by the group solver (place_group kitchen_run) before the agent is asked to relayout; the agent must not be asked to relayout a room whose program is incomplete.

a floor lamp whose generated model has a.rule: A floor lamp whose generated model has a shade at head height (blocking the view) must be swapped to a library model whose shade top is below 1.50 m; the fit stage must reject generated floor-lamp models whose shade exceeds 1.50 m.

a washbasin drawn within 0.50 m of a win.rule: A washbasin drawn within 0.50 m of a window/door that it blocks must be moved by the fit stage to the nearest free wall span; if no free span exists within 0.50 m, the drawing conflict is flagged for the architect.

a living room larger than 30 m2 must hav.rule: A living room larger than 30 m2 must have its seating and dining groups placed by the group solver before the agent is asked to relayout; the agent must not be asked to relayout a room whose program groups are missing.

a shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling mu.rule: A shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling must be swapped to a library model whose height is at most 2.80 m and whose style matches the project; the fit stage must reject models that fail the sloped-ceiling height cap.

the architect's rule f5 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F5 must explicitly list the cases where F9 (overlap) is acceptable (e.g. kitchen counters that share a wall) or the critic must not flag them.

the architect's rule s4 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule S4 must explicitly list the cases where G10 (clear in front) is acceptable (e.g. bathtub in a small bathroom) or the critic must not flag them.

the architect's rule f4 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F4 must explicitly list the cases where F6 (free zone blocked) is acceptable (e.g. armchair in a corner) or the critic must not flag them.

the architect's rule f3 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F3 must explicitly list the cases where G12 (piece in front of window) is acceptable (e.g. wardrobe under a high window) or the critic must not flag them.

an interior view of a small room (under.rule: An interior view of a small room (under 6 m2) must be posed to show the room's main furniture; if no free pose exists, the view is removed.

exterior views must not use low-poly lol.rule: Exterior views must not use low-poly lollipop trees; if no high-quality tree model is available, the site trees are set to 0.

interior views looking out a window must.rule: Interior views looking out a window must not use a flat, low-poly cartoon landscape; if no high-quality backdrop is available, the site trees are set to 0 and the ground is set to a neutral look.

a kitchen counter that cuts a wall by mo.rule: A kitchen counter that cuts a wall by more than 0.030 m must be moved by the fit stage to the nearest valid spot; if no valid spot exists within 0.50 m, the drawing conflict is flagged for the architect.

the exterior landscape must use the site.rule: The exterior landscape must use the site's real tree models, not the low-poly placeholder stand-in, so that views through windows read as a real garden.

a washbasin model must carry its own fau.rule: A washbasin model must carry its own faucet and mirror-ready top; a bare basin shell is a placeholder, not a finished fixture.

a bathtub model must include its fitting.rule: A bathtub model must include its fittings (faucet, shower head) in the asset; a bare tub shell is a placeholder.

sanitary ware must match the room's stat.rule: Sanitary ware must match the room's stated style; a dated two-piece model in a modern tiled bathroom is a mismatch.

a kitchen run must be built as a designe.rule: A kitchen run must be built as a designed run with handles, material variation and appliance integration, not as a row of blank parametric boxes.

a seating group must not be four identic.rule: A seating group must not be four identical chairs; the set needs variety in form and colour to read as designed.

a dining table must match the room's pal.rule: A dining table must match the room's palette and the seating set; a plain boxy slab is a placeholder.

a coffee table must match the room's pal.rule: A coffee table must match the room's palette; a third clashing wood tone is a mismatch.

chairs at one table must be the same mod.rule: Chairs at one table must be the same model; mixing two models reads as a mismatched set.

armchairs placed side by side must form.rule: Armchairs placed side by side must form a set; different models, colours and styles are a mismatch.

a bathroom must be styled with its full.rule: A bathroom must be styled with its full set (mirror, towel, soap, hardware); a bare washbasin is a placeholder.

a dresser model must have drawer lines,.rule: A dresser model must have drawer lines, texture and a top surface; a plain white box with floating dots is a placeholder.

a nightstand model must match the room's.rule: A nightstand model must match the room's wood tone and finish; a plain box in a clashing warm wood is a wrong model, not a placement problem.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main functional group, not a blank corner or a single fixture up close.

the exterior site must use realistic tre.rule: The exterior site must use realistic tree models and a textured ground plane, not low-poly placeholder 'lollipop' trees on a flat green plane.

sanitary fixtures must use styled, moder.rule: Sanitary fixtures must use styled, modern models that match the room's design aesthetic, not generic 'hospital' or 'construction site' models.

a washbasin must be a styled, modern mod.rule: A washbasin must be a styled, modern model that matches the room's aesthetic, not a plain utility sink with exposed chrome pipes.

an office chair in a bedroom must be a s.rule: An office chair in a bedroom must be a styled model that matches the room's soft, light-wood aesthetic, not a generic black utilitarian model.

a desk in a bedroom must be a styled mod.rule: A desk in a bedroom must be a styled model that matches the room's quality and aesthetic, not a plain, thin-topped placeholder.

a double bed must have a nightstand on b.rule: A double bed must have a nightstand on both sides; if the schedule lists two, both must be present and symmetric.

paired armchairs must be the same model.rule: Paired armchairs must be the same model or a coherent set; mismatched styles (white molded shell vs. grey upholstered wing) look like a random selection.

a floor lamp must have correct scale and.rule: A floor lamp must have correct scale and proportion; a shade that is too large and sits at head height, blocking a window, is a wrong model.

a hall/entrance must have an entrance gr.rule: A hall/entrance must have an entrance group (shoe cabinet, console, lighting) to look like a designed entrance, not a bare shell.

a stair and its railing must use a model.rule: A stair and its railing must use a model that expresses the project's style, not a plain, generic system that looks like a default placeholder.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main pieces and layout, not be too close to a corner and cut off the main furniture.

doors must be built with a frame, a hand.rule: Doors must be built with a frame, a handle and a leaf texture that matches the project's door material slot; a bare flat slab is a placeholder and must be rejected at the render check.

the main entrance door must be built wit.rule: The main entrance door must be built with a frame, handle and leaf texture matching the project style; a generic flat white slab is a placeholder.

a living room's seating group must be so.rule: A living room's seating group must be solved as one set (sofas, coffee table, rug) anchored on the drawn sofa, not as independent pieces placed by the fitter.

the exterior visible through windows mus.rule: The exterior visible through windows must use the site's real trees and ground, not a placeholder low-poly landscape.

a bathroom's set (bathtub, toilet, washb.rule: A bathroom's set (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) must be solved as one group so no member is missing or crammed into a corner.

a toilet model must match the style of t.rule: A toilet model must match the style of the bathroom's other fixtures (bathtub, tiles) to form a coherent set.

a bedroom's work group (desk, office cha.rule: A bedroom's work group (desk, office chair) must be solved as one set matching the room's style, not as independent generic pieces.

a bedroom's chest group (dresser, wardro.rule: A bedroom's chest group (dresser, wardrobe) must be solved as one set matching the room's style and scale, not as independent oversized pieces.

a bedroom's sleeping group (bed, nightst.rule: A bedroom's sleeping group (bed, nightstands) must be solved as one set with matching models and scales, not as independent mismatched pieces.

an interior camera must show the room's.rule: An interior camera must show the room's main fixtures, not be pressed against a wall or glass panel.

a door or window leaf that renders as a.rule: A door or window leaf that renders as a flat, untextured slab is a material-slot failure: the door and window_frame slots must carry a real finish (wood, painted or metal) from the style, never the default grey.

an interior camera that frames an open s.rule: An interior camera that frames an open stairwell edge or a floating landing reads as a safety/logic failure; the hall view must be posed to show the hall's furniture and doors, not the unguarded stair opening.

a small hall/corridor view aimed at a co.rule: A small hall/corridor view aimed at a corner and a door leaf reads as an empty, unstyled space; the camera must be posed to show the room's anchor (its furniture) and the door, not a bare wall.

a bedroom render that shows a sofa and n.rule: A bedroom render that shows a sofa and no bed is a furniture-placement failure: the room's bed must be the anchor the camera shows, and a sofa is not a substitute for the sleeping group.

a view dominated by a blank wall and a d.rule: A view dominated by a blank wall and a door leaf is unbalanced; the camera must be posed to show the room's furniture, with the door as context, not the subject.

a dressing-room camera pressed against t.rule: A dressing-room camera pressed against the wardrobe shows a wall and door leaf instead of the room; the view must be posed from a free point to show the room's door and its storage.

a decor cushion that penetrates its host.rule: A decor cushion that penetrates its host by more than 0.03 m is not rested and is dropped; the seating agent must re-seat it on the host's top surface.

a sideboard or console pushed into a cor.rule: A sideboard or console pushed into a corner with a large empty wall beside it is an unbalanced composition; the storage agent must re-place it along a wall span that balances the room.

an armchair pushed flat against a wall u.rule: An armchair pushed flat against a wall under a window instead of being part of the seating arrangement looks staged; the seating agent must pull it into the group.

a washbasin that reads as a floating sla.rule: A washbasin that reads as a floating slab with an unclear wall/counter relationship is a fixture-anchoring failure; the bathroom agent must re-anchor it to the wall or counter at working height.

a ground that renders as a flat, untextu.rule: A ground that renders as a flat, untextured green plane is a material-slot failure: the ground slot must carry a real ground look (grass, paving, gravel), never the default viewport floor.

exterior backdrop quality (flat ground,.rule: Exterior backdrop quality (flat ground, lollipop trees, low-detail sky) is a global render/scene setting, not a per-opening geometry defect; do not file it against a specific window or opening.

the exterior scene must use a textured g.rule: The exterior scene must use a textured ground and a realistic tree count (not lollipop placeholders) so the site reads as a believable landscape, not a flat backdrop.

a fridge (or any appliance) must use a l.rule: A fridge (or any appliance) must use a library model with sufficient mesh detail (>= 3000 triangles); a crude low-poly box is a placeholder and must be swapped for a detailed model of the same footprint.

a lone or unstyled cushion is a decor/st.rule: A lone or unstyled cushion is a decor/styling preference, not a geometry defect of the host sofa; do not file it against the sofa piece.

in a large living room, the dining group.rule: In a large living room, the dining group must be placed in a usable position (not shoved against a glazed wall with awkward chair angles) so the open floor is used sensibly.

a flat, low-quality view outside a windo.rule: A flat, low-quality view outside a window is a global exterior/backdrop render setting, not a per-opening defect; fix it once via the exterior scene, not per window.

a drawn piece that an ai pass names with.rule: A drawn piece that an AI pass names with a type fitting its size and room must be typed and built, not discarded as a 'detail' of a neighbouring piece.

the reading stage must read attdef (attr.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities in DWG files and pass their text values to the ledger, so that attribute-driven labels (room names, areas, notes) are not silently dropped.

site decor symbols read on an upper leve.rule: Site decor symbols read on an upper level that duplicate the ground plan's symbols at the same location are not separate site elements and need not be used; only unique L0 site decor is required.

when a room outline holds two distinct l.rule: When a room outline holds two distinct labels (e.g. a living room and a named dining zone), the reading stage must split the outline into separate rooms so each labelled space is its own room in the model.

the reading stage must capture printed a.rule: The reading stage must capture printed area labels (e.g. '9,00 m2') for each named space and pass them to the ledger so the area check can compare the drawn area against the modelled area.

when the reading stage chooses a wall la.rule: When the reading stage chooses a wall layer by evidence (closure rate, stroke pairing) and documents the runner-up and the primitives left out, the choice is valid and the left-out primitives are not a lost-element finding.

site decor symbols read on an upper leve.rule: Site decor symbols read on an upper level that duplicate the ground plan's symbols at the same location are not separate site elements and need not be used.

the reading stage must account for every.rule: The reading stage must account for every named layer in the DWG: if a layer's name indicates a fixture (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' = bathtub) and its geometry is not used by the model, the ledger must flag it so the fixture's drawn outline is checked against the built piece.

when a reading records the same opening.rule: When a reading records the same opening twice (duplicate evidence) and the build stage cannot resolve the duplicate, the build must keep the opening at its drawn position and flag the duplicate for review; it must not drop the opening from the model.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading stage must split the outline into two rooms at the wall that separates them, rather than keeping the largest label and discarding the other.

when a bed_double is placed under a slop.rule: When a bed_double is placed under a sloped ceiling and the render check sees it as a bed_single, the fit stage must verify that the bed's height and the ceiling clearance are consistent with a double bed, and if not, adjust the bed model or the ceiling height.

when a drawn piece is more than 0.3 m fr.rule: When a drawn piece is more than 0.3 m from its drawn place and the move is refused by the drawn_lock rule, the layout stage must check whether the piece's drawn position is valid (not in a wall, not blocking a door) and if so, allow the move; if the drawn position is invalid, the reading stage must correct the drawn position.

a room of 3.1 m2 with a single shoe cabi.rule: A room of 3.1 m2 with a single shoe cabinet and no other furniture is a storage/utility space, not a hall; the reading should type it storage.

elevation-to-plan opening checks must be.rule: Elevation-to-plan opening checks must be skipped (not flagged as a failed check) when the elevation has no north arrow or view bearing to orient it against the plan.

a drawn section is only checked point-by.rule: A drawn section is only checked point-by-point against the roof when its ends align with the roof outline within 0.30 m; otherwise the check is skipped and the section is left for manual review.
a drawn section is only checked point-by.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

elevation-to-model comparison is skipped.rule: Elevation-to-model comparison is skipped for any elevation that has neither a view bearing nor a side, and is not reported as a failed check.

when a dining group has no candidate pos.rule: When a dining group has no candidate position that fits the room's free spans, the solver must stop after the first refusal and leave the group for review instead of retrying the same span.

when an entrance group has no candidate.rule: When an entrance group has no candidate position that fits the room's free spans, the solver must stop after the first refusal and leave the group for review instead of retrying other spans.

when no library model of the building's.rule: When no library model of the building's window family fits an opening's size, the opening is built parametric in the style's finish and the finding is closed as a known library gap, not a defect.

a sink_kitchen built as a parametric mes.rule: A sink_kitchen built as a parametric mesh should be swapped to a library model of the same type when one fits the piece's size and the room's style.

a wall_cabinet built as a parametric mes.rule: A wall_cabinet built as a parametric mesh is a known library gap when no library model of the same type fits the piece's size; the finding is closed as a gap, not a defect.

a wardrobe whose model looks plain and i.rule: A wardrobe whose model looks plain and institutional should be swapped to a library model of the same type that matches the project's scandinavian/modern style.

a shoe_cabinet whose model looks plain a.rule: A shoe_cabinet whose model looks plain and boxy should be swapped to a library model of the same type that matches the project's minimal/modern style.

a door whose model looks plain and gener.rule: A door whose model looks plain and generic is a known library gap when no library model of the same type and style is available; the finding is closed as a gap, not a defect.

flat, untextured white wall surfaces tha.rule: Flat, untextured white wall surfaces that read as bare material should be given a textured plaster look to avoid a cheap, institutional appearance.

a stone path that looks like a rough, un.rule: A stone path that looks like a rough, untextured placeholder should be given a paving_stone look to read as a finished surface.

an office_chair whose model looks unfini.rule: An office_chair whose model looks unfinished and out of step with the room's lighter oak should be swapped to a library model of the same type that matches the room's style.

when a door opens onto a site area (balc.rule: When a door opens onto a site area (balcony, veranda) that the build stage left unbuilt (no outline), the render shows a bare default terrace; the fix is to build the site area's outline and railing, not to restyle the door.

interior doors of one house should share.rule: Interior doors of one house should share a single door material look so they read as a matched set; a generic mixed wood tone breaks the set.

a plain flat wood slab door clashes with.rule: A plain flat wood slab door clashes with a modern glass-and-metal interior; the door material should match the house's finish palette.

windows must render with a visible frame.rule: Windows must render with a visible frame and glazing (not a black void); the window_frame material must be a real frame look, not a dark void.

opaque dark windows make the house feel.rule: Opaque dark windows make the house feel cold; the window frame/glazing material should allow interior light to read.

an opening read twice and merged into on.rule: An opening read twice and merged into one is not a loss; the conservation check should not flag a deduplicated opening that remains in the final list.

drawing annotations (axis bubbles, grid.rule: Drawing annotations (axis bubbles, grid labels, level marks) are not building elements and should not be flagged as lost when not built.

cushions/pillows drawn on a host piece a.rule: Cushions/pillows drawn on a host piece are details of that piece, not separate furniture; they should not be flagged as lost.

cushions/pillows that are part of a libr.rule: Cushions/pillows that are part of a library model are not separate drawn pieces; they should not be flagged as lost.

axis labels are drawing annotations, not.rule: Axis labels are drawing annotations, not building elements; not building them is correct.

columns that are built as part of a site.rule: Columns that are built as part of a site structure (veranda posts) are not lost; the conservation check should credit them to the structure.

level marks are drawing annotations, not.rule: Level marks are drawing annotations, not building elements; not building them is correct.

exterior area labels are text annotation.rule: Exterior area labels are text annotations; their surfaces are built from site materials, so the label itself is not a lost element.

a kitchen counter read twice and built o.rule: A kitchen counter read twice and built once is a correct deduplication, not a loss.

a piece drawn inside another piece (high.rule: A piece drawn inside another piece (high overlap) is a duplicate or part, not a separate element to build.

a kitchen run drawn as one outline is co.rule: A kitchen run drawn as one outline is correctly decomposed into its counter segments and fixtures; the outline itself is not a lost element.

a drawn outline that encloses a group of.rule: A drawn outline that encloses a group of pieces and has no thickness of its own is a rug or zone boundary, not a furniture piece; it is not built as a piece.

a small drawn mark (under 0.30 m on a si.rule: A small drawn mark (under 0.30 m on a side) that lies inside a larger piece's footprint is a detail of that piece (cushion, pillow, seam), not a separate piece.

a piece removed by the ai's remove_piece.rule: A piece removed by the AI's remove_piece action is a deliberate design decision; it is not a lost element unless the documents show it is required.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side in a bedroom or living room is a built-in or long furniture run (desk, window seat, storage); it should be split into its constituent pieces or built as a custom run, not discarded as a group.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.20 m on a si.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.20 m on a side that fits no furniture type is a detail (tap, valve, threshold, shelf line), not a piece.

a small drawn mark (under 0.50 m on a si.rule: A small drawn mark (under 0.50 m on a side) that lies inside a larger piece's footprint (60% or more) is a detail of that piece, not a separate piece.

a nightstand that cannot be placed withi.rule: A nightstand that cannot be placed within 1.0 m of the bed after a bed resize should be re-placed in the next furniture round, not discarded.

the upper end of a stair that arrives fr.rule: The upper end of a stair that arrives from a lower level is not built again on the upper level if there is no level above; it is a single stair element spanning both levels.

a decor item that rests on a host piece.rule: A decor item that rests on a host piece is not built if the host is not built; it is a consequence of the host's removal, not a separate loss.
A decor item that rests on a host piece is not built if the host is not built; it is a consequence of the host's non-construction, not a separate loss.

a door symbol on a symbol layer that dup.rule: A door symbol on a symbol layer that duplicates an already-built door is a redundant symbol, not a lost element; do not flag it as a conservation loss.

hatch entities on a tarama/hatch layer a.rule: Hatch entities on a TARAMA/hatch layer are drawing annotations, not buildable elements; they are never a conservation loss when not built.

a drawn outdoor-space edge or step that.rule: A drawn outdoor-space edge or step that is already carried by a built veranda/balcony element is not a loss; the annotation is satisfied by the built element.

anchor the building frame to the drawn o.rule: Anchor the building frame to the drawn outer wall faces, not to the sheet outline corner; when the outer wall does not start at the sheet corner, apply the offset so all region and sheet coordinates are read relative to the true outer wall.

when a section prints the ground floor a.rule: When a section prints the ground floor at a non-zero datum (e.g. +0.50), read all plan relative marks against the building's true ground level (z 0), not the section's printed datum, so heights are not shifted by the datum offset.

a small drawn piece surrounding a level-.rule: A small drawn piece surrounding a level-mark text is a level-mark symbol, not furniture; it is correctly moved to symbols and not built.

when a document names a fixture in a roo.rule: When a document names a fixture in a room and the room's program already includes that fixture type, the furniture agent must place and verify it at the named location in its next round rather than leaving it unverified.

when a document names a dresser in a bed.rule: When a document names a dresser in a bedroom and the room's program includes a dresser, the furniture agent must place and verify it at the named location in its next round.

When a document names a dresser in a bedroom, the furniture agent must add and place a dresser in that room at or near the named location in its next round, even if the room's current piece list omits it.

when a document marks a dining zone in a.rule: When a document marks a dining zone in a living room and the room's program includes a table_dining, the furniture agent must place and verify the dining set at the marked zone in its next round, resolving any walkway conflicts.

a small seat drawn adjacent to and facin.rule: A small seat drawn adjacent to and facing a dining table is correctly typed as a chair by context; no retype is needed.

when a document names a dresser in a bed.rule: When a document names a dresser in a bedroom and no drawn dresser is at the named location, the furniture agent must add a dresser to that room in its next round, placing it at the nearest valid spot to the named location.

a warning that an opening is 'no passage.rule: A warning that an opening is 'no passage' because furniture stands across its approach is a false alarm when the opening is read as a window (sill >= 0.90 m); only true doors (sill at floor) need a clear approach.

a hall or corridor with an area below 3.rule: A hall or corridor with an area below 3 m2 is expected to have no furniture; a warning about missing furniture in such a room is a false alarm.

when two fixtures in a bathroom overlap,.rule: When two fixtures in a bathroom overlap, the smaller or more flexible fixture (e.g. washbasin) should be moved to a free spot, not the larger fixed one (e.g. bathtub).

furniture should not block the view or a.rule: Furniture should not block the view or access to a window; if a piece covers a window, it should be moved to a free spot.

a labelled veranda, terrace, or balcony.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace, or balcony in the documents must be built as a site area with a floor, and if columns or a roof are drawn, they must be included in the model.

a labelled veranda, terrace or balcony i.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace or balcony in the documents must be built as a site platform with its own outline, floor and railing, not dropped as 'no outline'.

an exterior door on an upper floor must.rule: An exterior door on an upper floor must have a built access (balcony, terrace, or external stair) that reaches its threshold.

a piece that overlaps another piece in t.rule: A piece that overlaps another piece in the same room is a fit failure: the layout stage must re-place it (or the room) so no two pieces intersect, before the render.

a kitchen room must be furnished as a co.rule: A kitchen room must be furnished as a complete run: the counter, the cooking zone (stove/hob) and the upper storage (wall cabinets) are one set; if the run is missing its cooking or storage members, the fit stage must complete the group rather than leave a bare counter.

a bedroom's secondary work group (desk,.rule: A bedroom's secondary work group (desk, office chair, and its supporting pieces) is part of the room's program; if the desk is listed but not built, the fit stage must place the work group rather than leave the room an empty shell.

a hall/entrance room's program includes.rule: A hall/entrance room's program includes its storage (shoe cabinet); if the listed piece is not built, the fit stage must place the entrance group rather than leave the corridor empty.

the exterior context seen through window.rule: The exterior context seen through windows must be a believable site (ground material, sky, and real trees), not a low-poly placeholder; the site stage must build the landscape to a renderable standard.

a living room's seating group must be a.rule: A living room's seating group must be a coherent set: matching sofas and a coffee table between them; if two mismatched sofas face each other with no table, the fit stage must re-solve the seating group as one unit.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a bare wall or door leaf; if the camera is aimed down a corridor and the room's furniture is out of frame, the camera stage must re-aim it to show the room's pieces.

An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a flat wall or wardrobe face; if the camera is pressed against a surface, the camera stage must re-aim it to show the room's pieces.

a scene check failure (s2) on a level in.rule: A scene check failure (S2) on a level indicates a geometry or placement error in the build stage; the build stage must be re-run to resolve the failed check.

a scene check failure (s3) on a level in.rule: A scene check failure (S3) on a level indicates a geometry or placement error in the build stage; the build stage must be re-run to resolve the failed check.

a kitchen counter must be against a wall.rule: A kitchen counter must be against a wall or integrated into the main run, not a freestanding block in the middle of the room; the fit stage must place the counter as part of the kitchen run.

a large living room (55.6 m2) must be fu.rule: A large living room (55.6 m2) must be furnished with its full program (seating, coffee table, storage, decor); if the room reads as barren, the fit stage must place the missing groups.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a bare untextured surface; if the frame is filled by a flat placeholder wall, the camera stage must re-aim it.

the exterior context must be a believabl.rule: The exterior context must be a believable site with ground material, sky, and landscape, not a flat untextured white void; the site stage must build the exterior to a renderable standard.

when a furniture-layer cluster in a bedr.rule: When a furniture-layer cluster in a bedroom is larger than 4.5 m on a side, the reading must split it into its individual drawn pieces (sofa, chairs, table) rather than leaving the strokes unassigned; a cluster that big is a group, not a single piece.

site areas labelled in the documents (ve.rule: Site areas labelled in the documents (VERANDA, BALKON) must be built as outlined structures (slab, railing, roof where drawn) from their site.paving/grass surfaces, not left as 'no outline'; a labelled site area is part of the building envelope.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side must be broken down into its individual pieces (by the reading or the build) and each piece built; a cluster is never left as a single untyped 'not built' element.

a site area labelled veranda in the docu.rule: A site area labelled VERANDA in the documents must be built as an outlined structure (slab, railing, roof where drawn) with its paving and furniture; it is not optional site decoration.

a site area labelled balkon in the docum.rule: A site area labelled BALKON in the documents must be built as an outlined structure (slab, railing, roof where drawn) on its level; it is not optional site decoration.

a bathroom render must frame the toilet;.rule: A bathroom render must frame the toilet; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a kitchen render must frame the dining s.rule: A kitchen render must frame the dining set; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a kitchen render must frame the upper ca.rule: A kitchen render must frame the upper cabinets; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a living room render must frame the dini.rule: A living room render must frame the dining set; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a piece listed in a room's program that.rule: A piece listed in a room's program that is marked 'not built' must be built (fitted and placed) before the run ends; a 'not built' flag on a program piece is a build failure, not a camera miss.

a dressing room render must frame the wa.rule: A dressing room render must frame the wardrobes; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toil.rule: A bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) must be placed with no overlaps; the solver must find a non-overlapping layout or the run must flag it as unresolved.

a window's sightline (ray through the op.rule: A window's sightline (ray through the opening) must not be blocked by furniture; the solver must place furniture clear of window sightlines.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.90-0.97 m); a counter built at 2.10 m is a misread size or a wrong model, and the build stage must reject or correct it.

an entrance area with stairs must have a.rule: An entrance area with stairs must have a clear, coherent layout: the main door, side door, steps, and handrail must form a legible sequence; the build stage must verify this coherence.

a door to a balcony or external landing.rule: A door to a balcony or external landing must have the balcony/landing built; if the site area is 'NOT built (no outline)', the door is a door into the air and the build stage must either build the landing or flag the door as unresolved.

a door read from a line in an outer wall.rule: A door read from a line in an outer wall at a level above the finished ground (z > 0.30 m) with no stair, ramp, landing or balcony outline reaching it is a misread: it is a window or a high opening, not a door; the reading must not emit a door for an outer-wall opening that no circulation reaches.

when the section prints the ground floor.rule: When the section prints the ground floor at a non-zero mark (e.g. +0.50), the reading must offset every relative level mark in the plans by that amount so that the building's z=0 matches the section's ground-floor mark; otherwise all relative marks are read 0.50 m lower.

an outer-wall opening that is fully or m.rule: An outer-wall opening that is fully or mostly blocked by furniture and has no outside access is a window, not a door; the reading must classify it by its approach, not its width.

when two built pieces overlap and single.rule: When two built pieces overlap and single-piece fixes are exhausted, the furniture agent must re-solve the room's set to resolve the clash.

a built piece covering a window opening.rule: A built piece covering a window opening is a real fit defect; the furniture agent must re-place the piece to clear the opening.

the big loop must run at least one full.rule: The big loop must run at least one full cycle before stopping; a deadline stop with 0 cycles and 303 open major points indicates the loop did not do its job.

views marked for review must be resolved.rule: Views marked for review must be resolved before the run ends; a view that shows a bare wall or a broken scene must be moved or removed.

the exterior scene must be photorealisti.rule: The exterior scene must be photorealistic; low-poly 'lollipop' trees and flat green planes are not acceptable for client-ready renders.

a washbasin model must have style and de.rule: A washbasin model must have style and design detail; a generic, featureless model makes the room look cheap and unfinished.

a kitchen counter must have handles, a p.rule: A kitchen counter must have handles, a proper countertop material, and a sense of a finished appliance run; a plain, featureless white box is not acceptable.

a kitchen must have a coherent run with.rule: A kitchen must have a coherent run with a hob, wall cabinets, and upper storage; a bare slab with a freestanding sink is not acceptable.

a fridge in a minimalist kitchen must ta.rule: A fridge in a minimalist kitchen must take a library model with a visible finish (stainless or panel), never the untextured parametric kitchen-run mesh.

a kitchen render must show a finished ru.rule: A kitchen render must show a finished run (handles, backsplash, appliances) and a dining set in one style; a grey-box massing with a mismatched chair is not client-ready.

a dining chair must match the table's li.rule: A dining chair must match the table's light-wood minimalist style; a dark heavy wooden chair is a style clash.

a stair must be built with a detailed mo.rule: A stair must be built with a detailed model (treads, stringers, handrail), never the untextured parametric solid block; the parametric stair is a placeholder that fails any client render.

a living room must read as one designed.rule: A living room must read as one designed set (matching sofas, chairs, table); a showroom of unrelated styles and a missing dining set is not client-ready.

an armchair in a minimalist salon must m.rule: An armchair in a minimalist salon must match the sofa's style and palette; a loud mid-century egg chair is a style clash.
An armchair in a minimalist salon must match the sofa's style and palette; a black mid-century shell chair is a style clash.

a sofa in a minimalist salon must match.rule: A sofa in a minimalist salon must match the other seating's style and palette; a long low orange sofa is a style clash.

a living room with two facing sofas must.rule: A living room with two facing sofas must have a coffee table or anchor between them and both sofas in one style; a caramel leather and a beige mid-century sofa facing each other with no anchor is not client-ready.

a dining table in a minimalist salon mus.rule: A dining table in a minimalist salon must match the room's light-wood style; a heavy wooden bench is a style clash.

the exterior landscape seen through wind.rule: The exterior landscape seen through windows must be a realistic, textured environment (real trees, hedge, path), never a low-poly lollipop placeholder.

a living room must read as one designed.rule: A living room must read as one designed set; a chaotic mix of styles and scales is not client-ready.

the exterior landscape seen through wind.rule: The exterior landscape seen through windows must be a realistic, textured environment, never a low-poly cartoon placeholder.

a washbasin in a monochromatic white bat.rule: A washbasin in a monochromatic white bathroom must match the room's palette; a stark glossy black box is a style clash.

a bathtub must be built with a detailed.rule: A bathtub must be built with a detailed model (curved rim, texture), never a plain white box primitive.

a bedroom with two beds must have both b.rule: A bedroom with two beds must have both beds in one style and the room composed with clear circulation; a white ornate metal frame and a plain modern frame are a style clash, and a camera too low and too close makes the room read as cluttered.

a room's furniture set must share one st.rule: A room's furniture set must share one style family; when two pieces of the same type in one room are from different style families, swap the one that is the outlier to a model from the family the rest of the room uses.

a wardrobe model must show visible doors.rule: A wardrobe model must show visible doors and hardware; a flat slab-like model with no front detail is not client-ready and must be swapped for a model with a finished front face.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture, not a railing, wall or door handle; if the current pose shows a non-furniture element in the foreground, re-aim it at the room's key pieces.
An interior camera must frame the room's main fixtures, not a wall, door handle or shower screen; if the current pose is blocked by a fixture, re-aim it to show the room's contents.

the outdoor environment visible through.rule: The outdoor environment visible through windows must be a believable landscape, not a low-poly placeholder; if the site has fewer than 6 trees or a flat untextured ground, increase the tree count and set a textured ground.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture, not a bare wall; if the room reads as a grey-box placeholder, re-aim the camera to show the key pieces.
An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture, not a bare wall; if the room reads as a half-finished shell, re-aim the camera to show the key pieces.

interior doors must match the room's woo.rule: Interior doors must match the room's wood tone; a darker, rawer wood door in a light-oak room clashes and must be set to a matching light wood look.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main features, not a blank wall; if the current pose wastes the frame on a wall and door, re-aim it at the room's key elements.
An interior camera must frame the room's contents, not a bare corridor ending on a door; if the room is a small hall, re-aim the camera to show its furniture.

exterior and window views must show a fi.rule: Exterior and window views must show a finished landscape (varied trees, hedge, path) and a textured ground, never the default low-poly placeholder set.

a bed model must include bedding and tex.rule: A bed model must include bedding and texture; a plain slab model is a placeholder and must be swapped for a styled one of the same type and size class.

a wardrobe model must show doors, handle.rule: A wardrobe model must show doors, handles and seams; a flat handle-less slab is a placeholder and must be swapped for a detailed model of the same type.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group, not be pressed against a single piece; the show list must include the room's key pieces.

two wardrobes in the same room must form.rule: Two wardrobes in the same room must form a coherent set (matching style, handles, finish); a mismatched model must be swapped for one that matches its partner.

a decor item that cannot rest on its hos.rule: A decor item that cannot rest on its host (penetration > 0.03 m) must be re-placed or removed in the next furniture round; it must not be left unbuilt.

a soft decor item (cushion, throw) that.rule: A soft decor item (cushion, throw) that cannot rest on its host within the penetration tolerance is dropped, not built floating; it is a minor cosmetic loss, not a missing element.

a sanitary fixture whose library model i.rule: A sanitary fixture whose library model is a plain untextured box should be swapped to a textured model of the same footprint to avoid the 'grey box' look in renders.

a fridge that is built as a sub-part of.rule: A fridge that is built as a sub-part of a kitchen_counter module and is not visible as a distinct appliance should be swapped to a standalone fridge model of the same footprint.

an exterior view that shows a flat empty.rule: An exterior view that shows a flat empty field with placeholder lollipop trees should have site items (trees, path, hedge) added to give the environment depth and realism.

an armchair pushed tight against a wall.rule: An armchair pushed tight against a wall with no breathing room should be re-laid out to give it clearance and a companion piece, so it reads as part of a seating arrangement.

a bed whose decor (pillows, throw) looks.rule: A bed whose decor (pillows, throw) looks unnatural or messy should be swapped to a model with better integrated styling.

a bed with plain, unstyled bedding shoul.rule: A bed with plain, unstyled bedding should be swapped to a model with richer integrated styling (throw, layered pillows) to read as a finished bedroom.

a camera view that does not show the mai.rule: A camera view that does not show the main furniture of a room should be moved to show them, so the room does not feel empty.

a ground that is a flat untextured plane.rule: A ground that is a flat untextured plane should be given a textured look (grass, paving, gravel) to give it realism.

a facade that is a flat untextured white.rule: A facade that is a flat untextured white surface should be given a textured look (plaster, brick, stone) to give it realism.

a stone cladding that is a flat untextur.rule: A stone cladding that is a flat untextured decal should be given a textured stone look to give it realism.

a drawn piece that is left out as a deta.rule: A drawn piece that is left out as a detail of a larger piece but whose size and AI naming fit a standalone furniture type should be retyped to that type so it is built.

the reading stage must read attdef entit.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF entities in DWG files, as they often hold room labels, dimensions, or other metadata needed for the model.

when a plan layer is named for a sanitar.rule: When a plan layer is named for a sanitary fixture (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' = washbasin) and its entities are not used by the model, the reading must map that layer to the corresponding fixture type and verify it against the built sanitary pieces, instead of leaving the layer unaccounted for.

when an opening is read twice (duplicate.rule: When an opening is read twice (duplicate) and the build stage cannot place it, the build stage must resolve the duplicate by keeping one instance at the read position rather than dropping the opening entirely.

a movable piece (armchair, sofa, table).rule: A movable piece (armchair, sofa, table) placed by the layout solver is not a misread of a drawn element; offset findings on movable pieces are layout noise, not reading errors, and should not be treated as misreads.

interior doors at the same floor level o.rule: Interior doors at the same floor level on both sides correctly have no threshold; a flush door leaf is the expected geometry, not a defect.

subjective aesthetic critiques of exteri.rule: Subjective aesthetic critiques of exterior composition (railing placement, flow) are not model errors; they are render/staging opinions that do not require a geometry fix.

balcony railing style and minor visual g.rule: Balcony railing style and minor visual gaps are aesthetic choices, not geometry errors; they do not require a model fix unless the railing is missing or structurally incomplete.

a room with an area below 3 m2 and no fu.rule: A room with an area below 3 m2 and no furniture or fixtures is a storage/utility space, not a hall; the reading stage should type small unlabeled rooms as storage by default.

a room with an area below 4 m2 and no fu.rule: A room with an area below 4 m2 and no furniture or fixtures is a storage/utility space, not a hall; the reading stage should type small unlabeled rooms as storage by default.

the reading stage must extract the north.rule: The reading stage must extract the north arrow (or equivalent orientation mark) from the drawing and use it to assign a bearing to each elevation, so that elevation-to-plan checks can run.

the reading stage must verify that a dra.rule: The reading stage must verify that a drawn section's cut line aligns with the plan's roof outline (within 0.30 m) before the section-to-roof check runs; if they do not align, the section is flagged as misread and the check is skipped with a clear reason.
the reading stage must verify that a dra.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

the reading stage must extract the north.rule: The reading stage must extract the north arrow and assign a bearing to every elevation; elevations without a bearing are flagged as unread and excluded from the model comparison with a clear reason.

a dressing room smaller than 8 m2 does n.rule: A dressing room smaller than 8 m2 does not need a full dressing group (vanity, mirror, seating); a wardrobe is sufficient for the room's function, and the layout solver is correct to skip the group when it does not fit.

when no library model fits a window's di.rule: When no library model fits a window's dimensions, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct fallback; this is a library gap, not a model error, and should not be flagged as a defect.

when a kitchen fixture is built parametr.rule: When a kitchen fixture is built parametrically because no library model fits, the fit stage should check for a close-size library model (within 10% of the drawn size) and use it if available, to avoid the 'below library level' warning.

when no library model fits a wall cabine.rule: When no library model fits a wall cabinet's dimensions, the parametric cabinet is the correct fallback; this is a library gap, not a model error, and should not be flagged as a defect.

when a dining table is built with a low-.rule: When a dining table is built with a low-poly or untextured model, the fit stage should prefer a library model with visible base detail and texture, even if it is slightly larger than the drawn size, to avoid the 'crude geometry' warning.

a living room's seating set carries one.rule: A living room's seating set carries one coffee table; a second identical table in the same zone is clutter, not a program, and is removed.

sanitary fixtures in a finished bathroom.rule: Sanitary fixtures in a finished bathroom take a minimal/modern catalogue model, not a generic default.

wet-room walls take a tile or stone look.rule: Wet-room walls take a tile or stone look, never a flat untextured white plaster.

the exterior site carries real trees and.rule: The exterior site carries real trees and a finished ground, not lollipop placeholders on a washed-out plane.

a bathroom camera frames the fixtures it.rule: A bathroom camera frames the fixtures it is meant to show; a view dominated by a glass screen that hides the toilet is re-aimed at the fixtures.

every fixture in a small bathroom must b.rule: Every fixture in a small bathroom must be fully in frame; a cut-off washbasin means the camera is re-aimed to include it.

a shower model must show its head and co.rule: A shower model must show its head and controls, not just a glass panel and wall.

a master bedroom bed takes a styled cata.rule: A master bedroom bed takes a styled catalogue model with headboard and bedding, not a bare low-profile platform.

two armchairs placed as a pair must be t.rule: Two armchairs placed as a pair must be the same model or a deliberately coordinated set.

a floor lamp in a soft-palette seating c.rule: A floor lamp in a soft-palette seating corner takes a low, warm model, not a tall slender tripod that overpowers the chairs.

a double bed's sleeping set carries a ni.rule: A double bed's sleeping set carries a nightstand on each side; a single nightstand with empty wall on the other side is a missing piece.

interior doors take a finished wood or p.rule: Interior doors take a finished wood or painted look, not a plain flat slab.

a nightstand in a calm, finished bedroom.rule: A nightstand in a calm, finished bedroom takes a styled catalogue model, not a plain open box.

window frames on a composed facade take.rule: Window frames on a composed facade take a warm wood or painted look, not identical narrow white plastic units.

outdoor furniture (veranda/terrace seati.rule: Outdoor furniture (veranda/terrace seating) takes a styled catalogue model in the project's exterior style, not a generic default 3D model.

an opening read twice from the documents.rule: An opening read twice from the documents and named in the evidence must be built; the build stage must not drop a double-read opening.

axis/grid bubbles and their labels are d.rule: Axis/grid bubbles and their labels are drawing annotations and are never built as building elements.

cushions and pillows drawn on a piece ar.rule: Cushions and pillows drawn on a piece are details of that piece and are not built as separate furniture.

cushions/pillows already part of a libra.rule: Cushions/pillows already part of a library model are not added again from the drawing.

columns drawn for a veranda/terrace are.rule: Columns drawn for a veranda/terrace are built as its posts, not as separate interior elements.

level/contour marks are drawing annotati.rule: Level/contour marks are drawing annotations and are never built as building elements.

exterior area labels are annotations; th.rule: Exterior area labels are annotations; their surfaces are built from the site paving/grass, not as separate elements.

a single drawn object read twice is buil.rule: A single drawn object read twice is built once, not as two pieces.

a piece drawn inside another piece (>=60.rule: A piece drawn inside another piece (>=60% overlap) is a part of it, not a separate piece.

a kitchen run drawn as one outline with.rule: A kitchen run drawn as one outline with its fixtures is built as its counter legs along the walls, not as one block.

an outline enclosing a group of pieces i.rule: An outline enclosing a group of pieces is a rug/zone outline, not a furniture piece.

a piece removed by the ai must be re-add.rule: A piece removed by the AI must be re-added if the room's program still requires it.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces and must be resolved into its constituents, not left untyped.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m on a sid.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m on a side is a line (threshold, shelf, valve), not a piece: it is not built and is not a loss.

a drawn element 60% or more inside anoth.rule: A drawn element 60% or more inside another built piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own: it is not built and is not a loss.

a nightstand drawn beside a bed that ove.rule: A nightstand drawn beside a bed that overlaps it must be re-placed in the free space at the bed's head, not dropped.

a piece removed by the ai's remove_piece.rule: A piece removed by the AI's remove_piece decision is not a loss; the conservation check records it as not built by design.

a stair's upper landing on the top floor.rule: A stair's upper landing on the top floor is not a separate piece; it is the same stair and is not built again.

a decor item whose host piece is not bui.rule: A decor item whose host piece is not built is not built either; it is a consequence of the host's absence, not an independent loss.

a door symbol on a drawing layer (kapi).rule: A door symbol on a drawing layer (KAPI) is an annotation, not a built door; it is not built and is not a loss.

hatch entities on annotation layers (tar.rule: Hatch entities on annotation layers (TARAMA, HATCH) are drawing symbols, not built geometry; they are never built and their absence is not a loss.

outdoor space details (edges, steps) tha.rule: Outdoor space details (edges, steps) that are built as part of a larger outdoor space element are not lost; the finding is a false alarm when the element is accounted for in the built space.

a consistent offset between the building.rule: A consistent offset between the building frame and the sheet outline is a coordinate datum, not an error; it is informational only.

when a section shows the ground floor at.rule: When a section shows the ground floor at a non-zero printed level (e.g. +0.50), the reading stage must apply that offset to all plan level marks so that relative heights (sills, thresholds, fixture working heights) are correct in the model.

small drawn pieces adjacent to level-mar.rule: Small drawn pieces adjacent to level-mark text are level-mark symbols, not furniture; they are correctly excluded from the build.

a furniture name text in the documents i.rule: A furniture name text in the documents is satisfied when the named piece type is already present in the room; no additional action is needed.

when a document-named piece cannot be pl.rule: When a document-named piece cannot be placed within the tolerance of its text label due to room geometry, the finding is a placement constraint, not a loss; it is handled by the placement solver.

a zone label in the documents is satisfi.rule: A zone label in the documents is satisfied when the corresponding furniture type is present in the room; no additional action is needed.

when a document-named piece cannot be pl.rule: When a document-named piece cannot be placed within tolerance of its text label, the furniture agent should attempt to place it at the nearest valid spot even if slightly beyond the text tolerance, rather than omitting it entirely.

when a drawn opening is blocked by a dra.rule: When a drawn opening is blocked by a drawn piece such that it cannot function as a door, and the opening's dimensions match a window (sill height, width), it should be read as a window, not a door.

a window (sill >= 0.90 m) in an outer wa.rule: A window (sill >= 0.90 m) in an outer wall is not a passage; furniture standing in front of it is not a blocked door and does not need a walkway.

furniture must not block the approach to.rule: Furniture must not block the approach to a door or window in a way that prevents its use.

a hall smaller than 3 m² does not requir.rule: A hall smaller than 3 m² does not require furniture.

furniture must not overlap other furnitu.rule: Furniture must not overlap other furniture.

furniture must not cover a window..rule: Furniture must not cover a window.

a labelled site area (veranda, balcony,.rule: A labelled site area (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be built as a platform with its own floor and edge, even if its surface is partially covered by the main building footprint.

a site area labelled 'veranda' or 'balko.rule: A site area labelled 'VERANDA' or 'BALKON' in the documents must be built as a covered or open terrace with a floor and a railing, not omitted or replaced by a flat roof.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) must be.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) must be adjacent to and accessible from a bedroom or bathroom, not a standalone room.

a room labelled 'oda' (room) that is sma.rule: A room labelled 'Oda' (room) that is smaller than 4 m2 and contains only a shoe cabinet should be typed as 'storage' or 'other', not 'hall'.

a hall on an upper floor must be connect.rule: A hall on an upper floor must be connected to the stair and to the rooms it serves. It should not be a dead-end.

a bathroom must be accessible from a hal.rule: A bathroom must be accessible from a hall or a bedroom. It should not be a dead-end.

a bedroom must be connected to a bathroo.rule: A bedroom must be connected to a bathroom or a hall that leads to a bathroom.

a piece that overlaps another piece in t.rule: A piece that overlaps another piece in the same room is a fit failure: the furniture round must re-place it clear of its neighbours before the render, not ship the overlap.

a kitchen room whose counter is built wi.rule: A kitchen room whose counter is built without its stove and wall cabinets is an incomplete kitchen run: the build stage must complete the run (counter + stove + wall cabinets) as one set, not ship a bare counter.

a room whose listed pieces (desk, office.rule: A room whose listed pieces (desk, office chair, armchairs, floor lamp) are absent from the build is a build loss: the furniture round must build every listed piece, not drop the secondary group.

a room whose only listed piece is absent.rule: A room whose only listed piece is absent from the build is a build loss: the furniture round must build every listed piece, even in a small hall.

a window view that shows a low-poly plac.rule: A window view that shows a low-poly placeholder landscape is a render failure: the exterior/site stage must provide a believable ground, trees and sky, not a grey-box lollipop scene.

two sofas of different styles facing eac.rule: Two sofas of different styles facing each other with no table between them is a fit failure: the furniture round must form a coherent seating group (matching set, table between) before the render.

a camera that frames a bare wall or door.rule: A camera that frames a bare wall or door instead of the room's main group is a render failure: the camera stage must aim at the room's content, not a dead-end corridor.

a camera pressed against a wardrobe face.rule: A camera pressed against a wardrobe face showing a flat surface is a render failure: the camera stage must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a wall.

a scene check failure on a level is a bu.rule: A scene check failure on a level is a build failure: the build stage must pass all scene checks before the render.

a kitchen counter placed freestanding in.rule: A kitchen counter placed freestanding in the middle of the room is a fit failure: the furniture round must place it against a wall or integrate it into the main run.

a large living room that appears empty i.rule: A large living room that appears empty in the render is a build loss: the furniture round must build every listed piece (coffee table, bookshelf, decor) so the room reads as furnished.

a camera that shows a bare untextured su.rule: A camera that shows a bare untextured surface is a render failure: the camera stage must frame the room's main group, not a placeholder wall.

an exterior view that shows a flat untex.rule: An exterior view that shows a flat untextured white void is a render failure: the exterior/site stage must provide a believable ground, sky and landscape, not a grey-box stage.

the site stage must build a believable e.rule: The site stage must build a believable exterior: a ground cover (grass or paving), a path to the entrance, and a scatter of trees (5-12) with a fence or hedge, never a flat untextured plane with lollipop trees.

a stove planned in the kitchen program m.rule: A stove planned in the kitchen program must be built with a dedicated stove model, not a kitchen_counter module model that may fail to instantiate as a separate object.

a fridge planned in the kitchen program.rule: A fridge planned in the kitchen program must be built with a dedicated fridge model, not a kitchen_counter module model that may fail to instantiate as a separate object.

an exterior camera view that must show a.rule: An exterior camera view that must show a specific window must be positioned to frame that window, not a blank wall or the opposite facade.

the reading stage must resolve all furni.rule: The reading stage must resolve all furniture-layer strokes in a room into typed pieces; a 0.56 x 1.20 m cluster in a bedroom is a sofa or a chair, not unassigned strokes.

when a room outline holds two labels (e..rule: When a room outline holds two labels (e.g. 'Mutfak' and 'ANTRE'), the reading stage must split the room into two, not merge the labels into one room.

a dresser named in the documents on a le.rule: A dresser named in the documents on a level must be built as a piece in the model; the reading stage must not drop named pieces.

a piece removed by the fit stage but sti.rule: A piece removed by the fit stage but still listed in the room program must be rebuilt, not left out.

a cluster of drawn pieces larger than 4..rule: A cluster of drawn pieces larger than 4.5 m on a side must be broken into its constituent pieces, not left as an untyped group.

a nightstand that is part of the sleepin.rule: A nightstand that is part of the sleeping set must be built, even if it was cut by the bed; the solver must find a free place within 1.0 m.

decor attached to a piece is lost if the.rule: Decor attached to a piece is lost if the host piece is not built; fixing the host fixes the decor.

a site area named in the documents (e.g..rule: A site area named in the documents (e.g. 'VERANDA') must be built with an outline, not left out.
A site area named in the documents (e.g. 'BALKON') must be built with an outline, not left out.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's principal fixture (toilet in a bathroom, bed in a bedroom, counter in a kitchen); a view that shows the room but not its anchor piece is a failed view, not a missing piece.

a bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toil.rule: A bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) must be placed so no two members overlap; when the drawn bays are too tight, the solver must re-place the set as a unit rather than leave a clash for the architect.

a window or door opening must have a cle.rule: A window or door opening must have a clear sight and passage line; furniture placed in front of an opening is a fit error and must be moved, not left to block the opening.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (about 0.90-0.97 m); a counter built with its top at 2.10 m is a build error and must be rebuilt at the correct height.

an entrance with steps must have a handr.rule: An entrance with steps must have a handrail that is connected to the steps and a clear relationship between the door, the landing and the steps; a disconnected handrail or unclear step-door relationship is a build error.

a dressing room (or any 'other' room tha.rule: A dressing room (or any 'other' room that is a suite component) must be directly connected to at least one bedroom or bathroom; a dressing room with no connection to a bedroom or bathroom is a layout error and must be flagged for the architect.

when a section prints the ground floor a.rule: When a section prints the ground floor at a non-zero mark (e.g. +0.50), the reading must anchor the building's level 0 to the section's datum and shift every plan mark by that offset, so relative heights stay true; a systematic level offset must be corrected at the level frame, not per element.

the exterior environment seen through wi.rule: The exterior environment seen through windows must be a finished landscape (real tree count, hedge or fence, ground cover), never the default low-poly placeholder.

a kitchen counter built as a bare parame.rule: A kitchen counter built as a bare parametric box (no hob, no wall cabinets, no upper storage) is an incomplete kitchen run; the run must be completed with its appliances and upper storage.

a fridge rendered as a plain untextured.rule: A fridge rendered as a plain untextured grey box (parametric kitchen_run module) must be swapped for a real library fridge model matching the room's style.

a dining chair whose style and colour cl.rule: A dining chair whose style and colour clash with the table and room (dark heavy wood in a light minimalist kitchen) must be swapped for a model matching the room's palette.

a staircase built as a solid untextured.rule: A staircase built as a solid untextured parametric block (no treads, no handrail) must be built with a detailed stair model (visible treads, risers, and a handrail) rather than a plain parametric box.

a living room whose seating pieces are f.rule: A living room whose seating pieces are from multiple clashing styles and colours (orange sofa, cream sofa, black chair, red egg-chair) must be re-fitted as a unified group with a coherent palette.

a statement armchair (red egg-chair) tha.rule: A statement armchair (red egg-chair) that clashes with the room's other seating must be swapped for a model matching the room's palette and style.

a sofa whose style and colour clash with.rule: A sofa whose style and colour clash with the room's other seating must be swapped for a model matching the room's palette.

a living room whose seating pieces are f.rule: A living room whose seating pieces are from multiple clashing styles and colours must be re-fitted as a unified group with a coherent palette.

a dining/coffee table whose style and ma.rule: A dining/coffee table whose style and material clash with the room's other furniture must be swapped for a model matching the room's palette.

a sanitary fixture model must match the.rule: A sanitary fixture model must match the room's finish palette; a glossy black basin in an all-white bathroom is a placeholder, not a design choice.

a bathtub model must have visible detail.rule: A bathtub model must have visible detail and style; a plain white box reads as a 3D primitive, not a real fixture.

a children's room must have a coherent,.rule: A children's room must have a coherent, age-appropriate furniture set; mismatched bed styles and a low, close camera make the render client-unacceptable.

two beds in the same room must be from t.rule: Two beds in the same room must be from the same style family; a vintage metal frame and a modern frame do not belong together.

a wardrobe model must show visible doors.rule: A wardrobe model must show visible doors and handles; a flat dark-wood slab reads as a raw material panel, not finished furniture.

a camera view must not include non-sensi.rule: A camera view must not include non-sensical elements (like a railing in a bedroom) that clash with the furniture; the furniture set must be stylistically coherent.

a bed and its matching dresser must be f.rule: A bed and its matching dresser must be from the same style family; a classic spindle-style bed and a modern button-tufted dresser do not belong together.

a children's room must read as a designe.rule: A children's room must read as a designed space with age-appropriate, stylistically coherent furniture; a dated adult-style bed and a huge dark wood wardrobe clash with a clean Scandinavian floor.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's contents (shower, toilet, washbasin), not a wall and a door handle; the view must not be blocked by a shower screen.
A bathroom camera must frame the room's contents, not a wall and a door handle; the view must not be blocked by a shower screen or a door.

the outdoor environment visible through.rule: The outdoor environment visible through windows must be client-ready; a crude, low-poly placeholder with 'lollipop' trees and a flat green ground is not acceptable.
