a bedroom must be styled with textures a.rule: A bedroom must be styled with textures and additional furniture; a grey-box placeholder with flat, untextured plaster walls is not client-ready.
A bedroom must be styled with textures and additional furniture; a half-finished shell with bare plaster and empty floor is not client-ready. Doors must match the room's style.

doors must match the room's style; a dar.rule: Doors must match the room's style; a darker, rawer wood door with no visible frame or hardware detail clashes with a light-oak set.

a hall camera must frame the room's cont.rule: A hall camera must frame the room's contents (stair, landing, windows), not a blank wall and a door; the outdoor view must be client-ready.

the outdoor environment visible through.rule: The outdoor environment visible through windows must be client-ready; a crude, low-poly model of trees and grass is not acceptable.

an interior camera of a small hall or co.rule: An interior camera of a small hall or corridor must frame the room's furniture and at least one door, never a bare dead-end wall.

the exterior environment (ground, trees,.rule: The exterior environment (ground, trees, sky) must be a believable landscape, not a low-poly placeholder, in every render.

a bed model must include bedding and tex.rule: A bed model must include bedding and texture; a plain slab is not client-ready.

a wardrobe model must have doors, handle.rule: A wardrobe model must have doors, handles or detail; a flat handle-less slab is not client-ready.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture group, not be pressed against a wall or a single piece.

furniture in the same room or set must s.rule: Furniture in the same room or set must share a coherent style; mismatched pieces break the design.

exterior views must show a finished site.rule: Exterior views must show a finished site: textured ground, a path to the entrance, and real trees, not placeholder lollipops on a flat plane.

a decor cushion that penetrates its host.rule: A decor cushion that penetrates its host by more than 0.03 m is dropped rather than built; the host's seat height must match the cushion's base.

a bathroom fixture that renders as a pla.rule: A bathroom fixture that renders as a plain untextured box should be swapped for a library model with real form and finish.

a kitchen appliance that is invisible in.rule: A kitchen appliance that is invisible in the render (built as a module cut or hidden) must be swapped for a standalone library model so the full appliance run reads.

a single armchair pushed tight against a.rule: A single armchair pushed tight against a wall with no companion reads as floating; the seating group must be re-solved so the chair has breathing room and a partner.

a bed whose decor (pillows, throw) rende.rule: A bed whose decor (pillows, throw) renders unnaturally should be swapped for a library model with correctly styled bedding.

a bed with a plain white duvet and no la.rule: A bed with a plain white duvet and no layered pillows reads as unfinished; swap for a library model with styled bedding.

a bedroom camera that frames only the be.rule: A bedroom camera that frames only the bed and leaves the wardrobe/dresser out of view must be moved to show the full furniture set.

a facade that renders as flat untextured.rule: A facade that renders as flat untextured white with a thin low-res plinth must be given a real masonry or render look.

a stone plinth that renders as a flat de.rule: A stone plinth that renders as a flat decal rather than real masonry must be given a proper stone look.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece's footprint is a detail of that piece (a sink bowl, an appliance front, a lamp base) and is not a piece of its own, even when an AI pass names it a furniture type that fits its size; it is dropped as a detail, not lost.

the reading must read attdef (attribute.rule: The reading must read ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities in the source DWG and carry their text into the ledger, so that attribute-driven labels (room names, areas, door/window tags) are not silently dropped; an unread entity type is a loss, not a warning.

site decor read outside the walls of a l.rule: Site decor read outside the walls of a level other than the ground floor (L0) is not used by the model and is not a loss; the site belongs to the ground floor, and decor symbols that repeat the ground plan at the same place are duplicates, not missing site items.

when a room outline holds two labels (e..rule: When a room outline holds two labels (e.g. a living room and a dining zone 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ') and the documents name the second as a distinct space with its own area, the reading must split the room into two (living + dining) rather than keeping one label and dropping the other; a second label with a printed area is a room of its own.

a printed area label (e.g. '9,00 m²' for.rule: A printed area label (e.g. '9,00 m²' for 'HOL') must be used by the area check of that space; if the label is not used, the area check is lost and the reading must bind the printed area to the room's area check.

when walls are drawn as face lines on a.rule: When walls are drawn as face lines on a layer chosen by evidence (e.g. 'SIVA'), the reading must also read the runner-up layer (e.g. 'DUVAR') and any other wall primitives off the chosen layer, so that no wall is lost; a layer choice by evidence must not silently drop wall primitives on other layers.

a layer with a meaningful name (e.g. 'de.rule: A layer with a meaningful name (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' = washbasin) that holds entities (e.g. 34 LINE entities) must be read and used by the model or named in a warning; an unused layer with a fixture name is a loss, not a silent drop.

A layer with a meaningful name (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' = washbasin) that holds entities (e.g. 56 LINE entities) must be read and used by the model or named in a warning; an unused layer with a fixture name is a loss, not a silent drop.

an opening read twice (e.g. o_l1_001, 1..rule: An opening read twice (e.g. o_L1_001, 1.98 m wide) that is named in the evidence but gone after the build stage is a loss; the build stage must not drop an opening that the reading named, and a re-run of the build stage must restore it.

a bed_double model that looks like a bed.rule: A bed_double model that looks like a bed_single in a render (e.g. due to a low profile or a single-mattress appearance) must be swapped for a model that clearly reads as a double bed (two pillows, a wider frame) in the render.

a chair that is 0.07 m from its drawn pl.rule: A chair that is 0.07 m from its drawn place (tolerance 0.05 m) is within the practical tolerance for a small piece in a furnished room; the layout is correct and the render check tolerance is too tight for a 0.45 m chair.

a chair that is 0.08 m from its drawn pl.rule: A chair that is 0.08 m from its drawn place (tolerance 0.05 m) is within the practical tolerance for a small piece in a furnished room; the layout is correct and the render check tolerance is too tight for a 0.45 m chair.

a dresser that is 0.15 m from its drawn.rule: A dresser that is 0.15 m from its drawn place (tolerance 0.05 m) is within the practical tolerance for a 1.20 m piece in a furnished room; the layout is correct and the render check tolerance is too tight for a piece of this size.

a drawn piece whose built position is mo.rule: A drawn piece whose built position is more than 0.15 m from its drawn centre is a layout drift, not a tolerance miss: the layout stage must re-solve the piece against its drawn anchor (or the room's wall span) instead of accepting the solver's free placement, and the render check must flag any drift above 0.15 m for re-layout rather than only above 0.05 m.

every interior door must be built with a.rule: Every interior door must be built with a visible threshold (a 10-15 mm reveal or a flush threshold strip) and a frame that contrasts with the wall finish; the render stage must not present a door leaf flush with the floor and a frame indistinguishable from the wall as a finished joinery.

the entrance area must be clearly define.rule: The entrance area must be clearly defined: the steps, the door, and any railing must form a coherent approach. The site stage must ensure that railings are connected to the steps or the building, and the overall flow to the entrance is legible in the render.

balcony railings must be fully enclosed.rule: Balcony railings must be fully enclosed on all edges and use a material and style consistent with the building's finish; a simple metal tube railing is not acceptable for a stylish home. The site stage must ensure the railing model fully encloses the balcony edge and matches the building's material palette.

a room smaller than 4 m2 that is not con.rule: A room smaller than 4 m2 that is not connected to the entrance and contains only a shoe cabinet is a storage or utility space, not a hall. The layout stage must retype such rooms to 'storage' or 'other' and not label them as 'hall'.

a hall on an upper floor that is not con.rule: A hall on an upper floor that is not connected to the entrance is a circulation space, not an entrance hall. The layout stage must label it as 'hall' (circulation) and not imply it is the main entrance. The entrance is on L0.

a bathroom that is not connected to any.rule: A bathroom that is not connected to any bedroom or hall is inaccessible and must be flagged. The layout stage must ensure that every bathroom is connected to at least one bedroom or the main circulation space. If a bathroom is isolated, it must be reconnected or retyped.

a bedroom that is not connected to any b.rule: A bedroom that is not connected to any bathroom is acceptable if the building has a shared bathroom, but the layout stage must flag it for review. The finding is that the bedroom is not connected to a bathroom, which may be intentional (shared bathroom) or a layout error.

a washbasin that is clashing with other.rule: A washbasin that is clashing with other furniture must be re-fitted by the agent. The fit stage must ensure that the washbasin is placed clear of other pieces and within the room's usable area.

scene check s2 failures must be resolved.rule: Scene check S2 failures must be resolved by the agent. The fit stage must ensure that all scene checks pass before the render stage.

elevation checks that require a north ar.rule: Elevation checks that require a north arrow must be skipped if the north arrow is not present in the drawing. The reading stage must flag the absence of a north arrow and the check stage must not fail the elevation check for this reason.

a drawn section that does not run one-to.rule: A drawn section that does not run one-to-one with the plan (its ends are more than 0.30 m apart from the roof outline's ends along the cut direction) is not checked point by point against the roof; the roof is validated from its own roof_line entities instead.
a drawn section that does not run one-to.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

an elevation that has neither a view bea.rule: An elevation that has neither a view bearing nor a side recorded is not compared with the model; the reading must assign each elevation a bearing or side before the check can run.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) must hav.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) must have a dressing group (wardrobe, mirror, bench or similar) placed; if the solver finds no place, the room's layout must be adjusted (e.g. by moving the existing wardrobe) to make room for the group.

a window that has no library model of it.rule: A window that has no library model of its family at its size is built parametrically in the style's finish; this is acceptable and not a building error.

a kitchen sink that is built below the l.rule: A kitchen sink that is built below the library level (parametric mesh) should be swapped to a library model that fits its size and the room's style.

a wall cabinet that is built below the l.rule: A wall cabinet that is built below the library level (parametric mesh) should be swapped to a library model that fits its size and the room's style.

a dining table that looks like a low-pol.rule: A dining table that looks like a low-poly asset (simple, untextured cylinder) should be swapped to a library model with better geometry and base detail.

a living room should have only one coffe.rule: A living room should have only one coffee table; if there are two, the second one should be removed to avoid clutter.

a toilet that looks very basic and gener.rule: A toilet that looks very basic and generic should be swapped to a library model with better detail and a more modern appearance.

bathroom walls should have a subtle tile.rule: Bathroom walls should have a subtle tile texture or paint sheen to avoid looking like a 'grey box' render.

the outdoor scene visible through window.rule: The outdoor scene visible through windows and doors should have realistic trees, a fence or hedge, and a front court to avoid looking like a flat, washed-out placeholder.

a bathroom camera should show the main f.rule: A bathroom camera should show the main fixtures (toilet, washbasin, shower) clearly, without being obscured by glass screens or door frames.

a bed model whose height and finish matc.rule: A bed model whose height and finish match the room's stated style (japandi/scandinavian) should be preferred over a generic low-profile platform when the room is otherwise styled.

when two armchairs share a seating corne.rule: When two armchairs share a seating corner, the fitter should pick a matching pair (same model or a coordinated set) rather than two unrelated models.

a floor lamp's height should be balanced.rule: A floor lamp's height should be balanced against the seating it serves; a very tall slender lamp overpowers low armchairs, so a shorter japandi lamp is preferred in a soft, low room.

a double bed's sleeping group is incompl.rule: A double bed's sleeping group is incomplete with only one nightstand; the fitter should place a matching pair flanking the bed.

door finishes should be selected from th.rule: Door finishes should be selected from the project's material palette to match the room's style, not left as a default plain slab.

a nightstand's model should match the ro.rule: A nightstand's model should match the room's stated style; a plain open box with hard edges reads as cheap in a calm, finished room.

facade window sets should vary in size,.rule: Facade window sets should vary in size, mullion pattern or glazing to read as a composed elevation rather than a monotonous parametric grid.

outdoor furniture should be selected to.rule: Outdoor furniture should be selected to match the project's style and add to the 'stylish' feel, not left as a generic default model.

when an opening is read twice from the s.rule: When an opening is read twice from the same drawing entity, the build stage should merge the duplicate reads into one opening rather than dropping one.

structural grid bubbles, axis labels and.rule: Structural grid bubbles, axis labels and drawing annotations are not part of the built house and should be excluded from the build stage.

cushions, pillows or details drawn on a.rule: Cushions, pillows or details drawn on a piece are part of the piece's model and should not be built as separate elements.

cushions/pillows that are part of a mode.rule: Cushions/pillows that are part of a model's own geometry are not separate pieces and should not be built as separate elements.

columns that are part of a veranda's str.rule: Columns that are part of a veranda's structure should be built as posts of the veranda, not as separate elements.

level mark symbols are drawing annotatio.rule: Level mark symbols are drawing annotations, not part of the built house, and should be excluded from the build stage.

exterior labels for site areas are not p.rule: Exterior labels for site areas are not part of the built house; their surfaces are built from site.paving/parking/grass.

when two drawn outlines of the same fixe.rule: When two drawn outlines of the same fixed run overlap by more than 60%, the build keeps one and records the other as a duplicate, not a loss.

an outline drawn inside a built fixed ru.rule: An outline drawn inside a built fixed run (kitchen counter, bath panel) is a part of that run, not a separate piece; the build drops it without loss.

a single large outline that encloses a k.rule: A single large outline that encloses a kitchen run and its fixtures is decomposed into the run and its fixtures; the outline itself is not a piece.

a large flat outline that encloses a fur.rule: A large flat outline that encloses a furniture group is a rug or zone marker, not a piece; the build drops it and the decor stage may add a rug.

a small outline drawn inside a built sof.rule: A small outline drawn inside a built soft-furniture piece is a detail (cushion, pillow) of that piece, not a separate piece.

an ai.remove_piece decision that removes.rule: An AI.remove_piece decision that removes a piece whose type is allowed in the room and that the drawing shows must be reviewed; the piece is restored unless the drawing clearly does not show it.
An AI.remove_piece decision that removes a decor piece (potted_plant, floor_lamp) that the drawing shows and that is allowed in the room must be reviewed; the piece is restored.
An AI.remove_piece decision that removes a chair from a kitchen or dining room that the drawing shows must be reviewed; the piece is restored.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side in a bedroom is a long storage piece (wardrobe, sideboard) or a group of pieces; the build must type it or decompose it, not leave it untyped.

a drawn outline thinner than 0.2 m that.rule: A drawn outline thinner than 0.2 m that fits no furniture type is a mark (threshold, line, valve), not a piece; the build drops it without loss.

a small outline drawn inside a built bed.rule: A small outline drawn inside a built bed is a detail (pillow, headboard) of that piece, not a separate piece.

a nightstand that overlaps a bed is re-p.rule: A nightstand that overlaps a bed is re-placed to the nearest free spot beside the bed; if no spot is free within 1.0 m, the bed is shifted to make room. A bedroom with a double bed must have at least one nightstand.

an ai.remove_piece decision that removes.rule: An AI.remove_piece decision that removes a shoe_cabinet from a hall or entrance that the drawing shows must be reviewed; the piece is restored.
An AI.remove_piece decision that removes a desk from a bedroom that the drawing shows must be reviewed; the piece is restored.
An AI.remove_piece decision that removes an office_chair from a room that has a desk must be reviewed; the piece is restored.

when a furniture name text names a piece.rule: When a furniture name text names a piece type and no drawn piece of that type stands within 1 m of the text, add the piece at the text's position if the room allows the type and the spot is free, instead of dropping it because the nearest valid place is more than 1 m away.

an outer-wall opening that is blocked by.rule: An outer-wall opening that is blocked by a drawn piece standing across its full approach (no free passage) and is read with a high sill is a window, not a door: the reading must classify it as a window at the floor's sill, not a sliding door.

a drawn bathtub that overlaps a neighbou.rule: A drawn bathtub that overlaps a neighbouring piece by more than tolerance is a misread size or position: the fixture must be resized to its real product size and/or moved to the nearest valid spot so it does not clash.

a piece that covers a window opening (do.rule: A piece that covers a window opening (door ray hits furniture) must be moved to a free place in its room, clear of the window.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcon.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a platform with its drawn outline, even if it is not a room.

a kitchen must have a dining set (table.rule: A kitchen must have a dining set (table and chairs) and a stove built and visible.

a bathroom must have a complete set (toi.rule: A bathroom must have a complete set (toilet, washbasin, and bathtub or shower) built and visible.

a bedroom must have a dresser or chest o.rule: A bedroom must have a dresser or chest of drawers built and visible.

a kitchen counter's top must be at a wor.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at a working height (0.85-0.95 m), not at 2.10 m.

a kitchen must have a stove built and vi.rule: A kitchen must have a stove built and visible.

a kitchen must have a fridge built and v.rule: A kitchen must have a fridge built and visible.

a kitchen must have wall cabinets built.rule: A kitchen must have wall cabinets built and visible.

a bedroom with two beds must have both b.rule: A bedroom with two beds must have both beds built and visible.

a bedroom must have a wardrobe built and.rule: A bedroom must have a wardrobe built and visible.

a kitchen must have a kitchen counter bu.rule: A kitchen must have a kitchen counter built and visible.

a kitchen must have a sink built and vis.rule: A kitchen must have a sink built and visible.

a kitchen must have a dining set (table.rule: A kitchen must have a dining set (table and chairs) built and visible.

a rule is needed to build site areas (ve.rule: A rule is needed to build site areas (verandas, balconies, terraces) that are named in the documents but lack a built outline. The site stage should generate a floor slab, railing, and roof overhang for any labelled outdoor area.

a scene check that fails on a level is a.rule: A scene check that fails on a level is a build-stage defect: re-run the build stage for that level so the geometry is regenerated and re-checked.

a washbasin in a bathroom must be built.rule: A washbasin in a bathroom must be built as part of a vanity unit (a cabinet or counter it sits on), never as a bare bowl on a shelf; when the room has no vanity, the bathroom set must supply one.

a dresser in a bedroom must be placed ag.rule: A dresser in a bedroom must be placed against a wall, never in the middle of the room as a partition; the furniture agent must re-place it to a free wall span.

a piece that the decor stage built must.rule: A piece that the decor stage built must not be dropped by the agent stage; if the agent removes it, the removal must be recorded and the piece rebuilt in the next round.

a fridge planned in the kitchen must be.rule: A fridge planned in the kitchen must be built as a standalone appliance, not as part of the kitchen_counter module; when the module build drops it, a library model must be assigned.

an exterior camera that must show a wind.rule: An exterior camera that must show a window must be positioned so the window is in frame; if the current pose misses it, the camera must be moved.

drawn strokes on the furniture layer tha.rule: Drawn strokes on the furniture layer that form a group (sofa, chairs around a table) must be resolved into individual typed pieces by the reading stage, not left as unassigned strokes.

when a room outline holds two labels, th.rule: When a room outline holds two labels, the reading stage must split it into two rooms; a wall between them must be read or created.

a piece named in the documents (by a tex.rule: A piece named in the documents (by a text label) must be built in the model; if the reading stage missed it, the agent stage must add it.

a piece removed by the agent must be reb.rule: A piece removed by the agent must be rebuilt if the room's program still lists it; the removal reason must not hide a loss.

a cluster of drawn pieces larger than 4..rule: A cluster of drawn pieces larger than 4.5 m on a side must be broken into its constituent pieces by the reading stage, not left as a single untyped piece.

site areas labeled as veranda or balkon.rule: Site areas labeled as VERANDA or BALKON in the documents must be built as outlined platforms or terraces in the 3D model, even if they are not enclosed rooms.

a dressing room must be directly connect.rule: A dressing room must be directly connected to a bedroom or a bathroom; if it is not, it should be merged into an adjacent room or its type changed to 'storage' or 'hall'.

the ground floor level mark in the secti.rule: The ground floor level mark in the section must be read as 0.00 m, not +0.50 m; all relative marks in the plans must be adjusted accordingly to avoid a systematic 0.50 m level error.

the big loop must run at least two full.rule: The big loop must run at least two full cycles before it may stop on a deadline, so that a first pass that only fixes geometry still gets a second pass to style and light the rooms.

a view that is marked for review must be.rule: A view that is marked for review must be re-evaluated in the next render cycle; a view left in review at the end of a run is a failed check, not a finished one.

when every candidate model for a wall-hu.rule: When every candidate model for a wall-hung washbasin is refused by the fit rules because the model's height exceeds the clearance under a sloped ceiling or a low fixture, the fit check must compare the model's height to the local ceiling clearance at the piece's position, not to a global cap, and must allow a model whose top is below that clearance.

When every candidate model for a wall-hung washbasin is refused by the fit rules because the model's height exceeds the clearance under a sloped ceiling, the fit check must compare the model's height to the local ceiling clearance at the piece's position, not to a global cap, and must allow a model whose top is below that clearance.

a floor lamp that is taller than the sea.rule: A floor lamp that is taller than the seating it accompanies in the same room should be swapped for a model whose height is within 0.3 m of the seat height of the nearest armchair or sofa, so the lamp does not tower over the seating group.

when a relayout of a room is refused bec.rule: When a relayout of a room is refused because it would leave a door-to-door walkway below 0.60 m, the solver must treat the walkway constraint as a hard constraint that overrides the desire to fill the room with furniture, and must leave the walkway clear even if that means the room looks emptier.

when a drawn piece is left unbuilt becau.rule: When a drawn piece is left unbuilt because its cluster is larger than 4.5 m on a side, the reading stage must split the cluster into individual pieces (e.g. a wardrobe and a dresser) rather than discarding the whole cluster, so that each piece can be built and placed.

an interior camera of a small room (unde.rule: An interior camera of a small room (under 10 m2) must be placed so that the room's main furniture (e.g. a wardrobe in a dressing room) is visible in the frame, not just a door and a sliver of the wall.

furniture placed on a terrace or balcony.rule: Furniture placed on a terrace or balcony must be a coherent set (e.g. a matching lounge set) rather than a random mix of different styles and types, so that the outdoor space reads as a designed area.

a bathroom render must include warm ligh.rule: A bathroom render must include warm lighting (e.g. a pendant lamp or wall sconce) and styled surfaces (e.g. a towel, a plant, or a decorative object) to avoid looking like a sterile grey box.

a bathroom must have at least one warm l.rule: A bathroom must have at least one warm light source (e.g. a pendant lamp, wall sconce, or under-cabinet light) in addition to the main ceiling light, to create a layered and inviting atmosphere.

an interior camera of a bathroom must be.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must be placed so that the main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, bathtub or shower) are visible in the frame, not cut off at the bottom or awkwardly positioned.

a kitchen render must include styled sur.rule: A kitchen render must include styled surfaces (e.g. plants, wall art, decorative objects on the counters) and warm lighting to create a cozy and lived-in atmosphere, not a sterile empty shell.

a kitchen must have at least one decorat.rule: A kitchen must have at least one decorative element on the counters (e.g. a plant, a fruit bowl, or a decorative object) and at least one wall decoration (e.g. a picture, a shelf, or a clock) to create a lived-in feel.

a dining chair must match the style and.rule: A dining chair must match the style and material of the dining table it accompanies, so that the dining set reads as a coherent group rather than a mismatched pair.

a kitchen render must include warm light.rule: A kitchen render must include warm lighting, styled surfaces, and a coherent furniture set to match the project's style, not a sterile empty shell with generic boxy cabinets.

appliance models (fridge, stove, washing.rule: Appliance models (fridge, stove, washing machine) must be selected from the catalogue by the project's style tag; if no model matches the style, the parametric family in the project's finish is used instead of a pinned modern model that clashes with the cabinetry.

washbasins under sloped ceilings must be.rule: Washbasins under sloped ceilings must be selected or mounted to fit the available clearance; if no catalogue model fits, a parametric vessel sink at the correct working height (rim at 0.85 m) is used instead of a crude placeholder.

a piece's model must match the room's pa.rule: A piece's model must match the room's palette and style: a dark glossy shell is refused in a light, airy room; the solver picks a model in the room's style family.

a children's room must be furnished as a.rule: A children's room must be furnished as a bedroom, not an office: the furniture set must be coherent and the desk placed sensibly.

two beds in the same room must be from t.rule: Two beds in the same room must be from the same design family: the solver picks matching models for a pair of beds.

a bathroom camera must show the room's m.rule: A bathroom camera must show the room's main group (washbasin, shower, toilet) in frame, not a close-up of a corner.

a bathroom must have styled surfaces (a.rule: A bathroom must have styled surfaces (a vanity with a vessel sink, a tray, and accessories) to match the reference.

a bedroom must be furnished with its ful.rule: A bedroom must be furnished with its full set of pieces (armchairs, desk, office chair, floor lamp) and styled to match the project's style.

a bedroom must have styled surfaces (thr.rule: A bedroom must have styled surfaces (throws, cushions, and a rug with texture) to match the reference.

two identical, plain wooden doors side-b.rule: Two identical, plain wooden doors side-by-side on the same wall is a design error; the agent must resolve the door placement.

a piece's model must match the room's pa.rule: A piece's model must match the room's palette and style: a modern molded plastic armchair is refused in a room with natural wood and neutral bedding.
A piece's model must match the room's palette and style: a neon pineapple lamp is refused in a room with a neutral and calm palette.

a bedroom must be furnished with its ful.rule: A bedroom must be furnished with its full set of pieces and styled to match the project's style.
A bedroom must be furnished with its full set of pieces (desk, office chair, armchairs, floor lamp) to look like a fully designed space.

a hall must have warm, layered, and fini.rule: A hall must have warm, layered, and finished quality (art, plants, rug, warm light) to match the reference.

a hall must have wall art to avoid dead.rule: A hall must have wall art to avoid dead zones that make the space feel unfinished and empty.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group, not a bare corner of door and wall.

a bedroom's bed wall must carry a headbo.rule: A bedroom's bed wall must carry a headboard or wall art; a large blank wall above the bed is an incomplete layer.

a finished bedroom render must carry the.rule: A finished bedroom render must carry the project's style layer (textiles, art, plants, warm light); a bare grey box is not client-ready.

interior doors must carry a finished mat.rule: Interior doors must carry a finished material (wood or painted), not a plain untextured slab.

an exterior render must carry the site l.rule: An exterior render must carry the site layer (planting, path, textured ground), not a flat green plane with lollipop trees.

when the reference shows a defined garde.rule: When the reference shows a defined garden (hedges, beds, a path), the exterior stage must build those site layers, not a flat untextured ground plane.

a decor cushion that penetrates its host.rule: A decor cushion that penetrates its host by more than the 0.03 m rest tolerance is correctly not built; the host's top surface must be re-seated so the cushion rests.

a desk in a bedroom must be placed for n.rule: A desk in a bedroom must be placed for natural light and a logical workflow (near the window or a working wall), not in a dead zone in the middle of a wall.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece's footprint is a detail of that piece and is not built as its own; an AI pass that names it a separate type (floor_lamp/nightstand) must not override that containment test, and the reading must not emit it as a standalone piece.

the reading stage must read attdef (attr.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities in a DWG, not skip them; they carry the text of block attributes (room labels, dimensions) that the ledger checks.

site decor read on a level other than th.rule: Site decor read on a level other than the ground floor (L0) is a duplicate of the ground plan's symbols and must be dropped by the site stage, not carried forward unused.

when a room outline holds two labels (e..rule: When a room outline holds two labels (e.g. a living room and a dining area), the reading stage must split it into two rooms at the wall between them, not merge them under one label.

a printed area label on a plan must be m.rule: A printed area label on a plan must be matched to its room and used for the area check; if the room's built area disagrees, the reading must flag it, not drop the label.

when walls are drawn as face lines on a.rule: When walls are drawn as face lines on a chosen layer, the reading stage must also check the runner-up layer and any off-layer wall primitives that close a labelled room, not leave them out silently.

a layer whose name denotes a building el.rule: A layer whose name denotes a building element (e.g. DENIZLIK = bathtub) must be read and matched to the corresponding fixture; if none of its entities are used, the reading must flag it, not drop it silently.

an opening read twice (duplicate evidenc.rule: An opening read twice (duplicate evidence) must be deduplicated by the build stage, not dropped; if it is gone after the build stage, the build must re-run to restore it.

when an elevation sheet lacks a north ar.rule: When an elevation sheet lacks a north arrow or side label, the pipeline must record the elevation's orientation from the plan's section cut line (its arrow direction) so that its openings can be checked against the plan; if no cut line is present, the check is skipped with an explicit 'orientation unknown' note rather than silently failing.

when a drawn section's ends do not align.rule: When a drawn section's ends do not align with the roof outline's ends (offset > 0.30 m), the pipeline must flag the section as 'not co-located with the plan' and skip the point-by-point roof check, recording the offset, rather than attempting a one-to-one comparison that will always fail.
when a drawn section's ends do not align.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

elevations without a view bearing or sid.rule: Elevations without a view bearing or side label must be assigned an orientation from the plan's section cut lines or from their position relative to the building's north arrow before the render comparison stage; if no orientation can be derived, the comparison is skipped with an explicit note.

when a dining group in a kitchen has no.rule: When a dining group in a kitchen has no valid placement on any free wall span (all candidates fail the checks), the solver must place it at the best-scoring candidate position (the one with the fewest violations) and flag it for review, rather than refusing all placements and leaving the group unbuilt.

when a drawn piece's decor cushion does.rule: When a drawn piece's decor cushion does not rest (penetration > 0.03 m) and the piece cannot be moved more than 0.3 m (drawn_lock), the pipeline must either (a) swap the piece to a model whose cushion rests correctly, or (b) mark the cushion as a known tolerance issue and suppress the not-rested warning, rather than leaving the piece unbuilt.

when a wall_cabinet is built with a para.rule: When a wall_cabinet is built with a parametric mesh (below library level) and no library model is listed in models_it_may_take, the pipeline must flag it as a library gap and either (a) generate a parametric model with the style's finish, or (b) accept the parametric mesh with a note, rather than leaving it as a silent taste issue.

a bed model that renders as a flat, unte.rule: A bed model that renders as a flat, untextured box with no headboard or legs is a placeholder; the fit stage must reject such low-detail models in favour of a detailed product of the same type and size.

a bed model that clashes with the room's.rule: A bed model that clashes with the room's reference style (a generic platform in a styled room) must be swapped for a model matching the room's style and size.

interior door leaves must be built with.rule: Interior door leaves must be built with a detailed, moulded model (panels, finish, handle) matching the project's door material slot, never a flat untextured slab.

a wardrobe whose flat, untextured finish.rule: A wardrobe whose flat, untextured finish reads as a placeholder must be swapped for a detailed product model of the same type and size; a generated model with guessed units is not an acceptable substitute when a real product fits.

the agent stage must not drop a drawn de.rule: The agent stage must not drop a drawn desk that the decor stage placed; if a desk is removed, the reason must be recorded and the piece restored or re-placed.

when a document names a storage piece (d.rule: When a document names a storage piece (dresser, chest, sideboard) at a position that is more than 1 m from any valid placement in the room, and the room already contains a wardrobe or tall cabinet, the named piece is treated as a duplicate of the existing storage and is not built; the finding is closed as a false alarm. If the room has no other storage, the piece is placed at the nearest valid spot regardless of the 1 m tolerance, and the finding is closed as fixed.

a furniture piece must not sit on the cl.rule: A furniture piece must not sit on the clear opening of a window or door: the door/window ray check must reject any placement whose footprint intersects the opening's clear width, and the fitter must push the piece to the nearest free spot clear of the opening.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrac.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrace, balcony) in the site plan must be built as a platform with its drawn outline, columns and glazing/railing; 'no outline' is a loss, not a valid reason to skip it.

a kitchen counter's top must be at worki.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at working height (0.85-0.95 m); a counter read at 2.10 m is a misread size, not a tall cabinet.

a kitchen room's program requires a stov.rule: A kitchen room's program requires a stove/hob; if the drawn stove is not built, the kitchen_run group must be completed with it.

a dining table in a furnished render mus.rule: A dining table in a furnished render must have styled surfaces (tablecloth, setting, or at least a centrepiece); a bare table is a missing layer.

a large blank wall behind a seating area.rule: A large blank wall behind a seating area in a living room must have wall art or a feature; an empty wall is a missing layer.

sofas and armchairs in the same seating.rule: Sofas and armchairs in the same seating group must be from a compatible design family; a clash of styles is a mismatched_set.

a dining set (table + chairs) must be a.rule: A dining set (table + chairs) must be a unified group; a single mismatched chair is a mismatched_set.

a fridge in a kitchen must match the kit.rule: A fridge in a kitchen must match the kitchen's material palette; a glossy black fridge in a matte warm kitchen is a mismatched_set.

a bedroom's listed pieces (desk, office.rule: A bedroom's listed pieces (desk, office chair, etc.) must be visible in the render; if they are missing after the agent stage, the agent must place them.

two beds in the same room must be from a.rule: Two beds in the same room must be from a compatible design family; different headboards are a mismatched_set.

armchairs in a bedroom must match the ro.rule: Armchairs in a bedroom must match the room's material palette; molded plastic in a warm neutral room is a mismatched_set.

a wardrobe listed in a bedroom's pieces.rule: A wardrobe listed in a bedroom's pieces must be visible in the render; if it is missing after the agent stage, the agent must place it.

a dresser listed in a bedroom's pieces m.rule: A dresser listed in a bedroom's pieces must be visible in the render; if it is missing after the agent stage, the agent must place it.

a washbasin in a bathroom must be on a p.rule: A washbasin in a bathroom must be on a proper vanity, not a small shelf; a low-poly black box is a placeholder, not a styled fixture.

a labelled veranda, terrace, or balcony.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace, or balcony in the site plan must be built as a distinct platform with a floor, a parapet or railing, and a door or opening from the adjacent interior room. If the outline is missing, the site stage must reconstruct it from the plan lines before the building stage.

a scene check failure on a level means t.rule: A scene check failure on a level means the build stage produced geometry that violates the level's constraints; rerunning the build stage regenerates the level geometry and re-validates it.

a washbasin that is placed awkwardly on.rule: A washbasin that is placed awkwardly on a small shelf next to the tub, not in a proper vanity unit, should be swapped for a model that includes a vanity unit or is designed to be wall-hung at the correct height.

a tall dresser placed in the middle of a.rule: A tall dresser placed in the middle of a room, acting as a bulky partition, should be swapped for a lower or slimmer model that does not block the flow of space.

a piece that is planned to be built but.rule: A piece that is planned to be built but has no object in the scene should be retyped to its correct type to force a rebuild with a suitable model.

a window that is not seen in a view that.rule: A window that is not seen in a view that must show it should be addressed by adjusting the camera to include the window in the frame.

drawing strokes on the furniture layer t.rule: Drawing strokes on the furniture layer that are not used by any piece should be checked for whether they represent furniture that was lost during the reading stage. If they do, the reading stage should be improved to recognize them.

a room that has a second label in the do.rule: A room that has a second label in the documents but is not a room of its own in the model should be split into two rooms during the reading stage.

a piece that is named in the documents b.rule: A piece that is named in the documents but has no corresponding piece in the model should be added to the model during the reading stage.

a piece that was removed by ai but is a.rule: A piece that was removed by AI but is a valid piece in the room should be retyped to its correct type to force a rebuild with a suitable model.

a cluster of drawn pieces that is too la.rule: A cluster of drawn pieces that is too large to be a single furniture piece and does not fit any type should be marked as not furniture with the evidence from the plan crop.

a piece that was not built because it cu.rule: A piece that was not built because it cut another piece and no free place was found within 1.0 m should be moved to the nearest free place in the room.

a piece removed by the ai that is a vali.rule: A piece removed by the AI that is a valid type for its room (a shoe cabinet in a hall) must be rebuilt by retyping it to its own type, not to a different type that fits its footprint.
A piece removed by the AI that is a valid type for its room (a desk in a bedroom) must be rebuilt by retyping it to its own type.
A piece removed by the AI that is a valid type for its room (an office chair in a bedroom) must be rebuilt by retyping it to its own type.

a piece that blocks a walkway must be mo.rule: A piece that blocks a walkway must be moved to a free place that clears the walkway, not removed.

a decor item that depends on a piece whi.rule: A decor item that depends on a piece which was not built must be resolved by rebuilding the host piece.

site areas labeled in the documents (e.g.rule: Site areas labeled in the documents (e.g., VERANDA, BALKON) must be built with an outline and structure if they are primary outdoor living spaces.
Site areas labeled in the documents (e.g., BALKON) must be built with an outline and structure.

a kitchen must have its main functional.rule: A kitchen must have its main functional anchor (stove/hob) visible and at working height on the counter.

a room's main functional pieces (desk, o.rule: A room's main functional pieces (desk, office chair, armchairs, floor lamp) must be visible in the render.

a bathroom's washbasin must be a proper.rule: A bathroom's washbasin must be a proper vanity, not a crude placeholder, and must be visible in the render.

a bathroom's washbasin must be visible i.rule: A bathroom's washbasin must be visible in the render and not a crude placeholder.

a room's main functional pieces (desk, o.rule: A room's main functional pieces (desk, office chair, armchairs) must be visible in the render.

a wardrobe must be visible in the render.rule: A wardrobe must be visible in the render and not block a door or window.

a dresser must be visible in the render..rule: A dresser must be visible in the render.

a dressing room must have a dressing are.rule: A dressing room must have a dressing area (e.g., a bench, a mirror, a rail) visible in the render.

a drawn bathroom fixture that overlaps a.rule: A drawn bathroom fixture that overlaps a partner fixture and has no free place within its move limits is a fit failure: the solver must re-solve the bathroom set as one unit around the drawn anchor rather than leaving the overlap open for the architect.

a piece that blocks the sightline or pas.rule: A piece that blocks the sightline or passage through a window opening must be moved or removed; the fit stage must check that no furniture stands in the clear zone of any opening.

a kitchen counter built with its top abo.rule: A kitchen counter built with its top above working height (0.97 m) is a fitting error: the parametric mesh was chosen without checking the vertical placement against the working-height rule.

an entrance with both a ramp and stairs.rule: An entrance with both a ramp and stairs competing for the same space is a build error: the entrance solution must be a single, coherent choice (steps, ramp, or none) that matches the site grade difference.

a room typed as 'other' with only a ward.rule: A room typed as 'other' with only a wardrobe is not a functional room type; it should be typed as 'storage' (or 'dressing' if the program supports it) to match its contents and area.

when a document names a piece (e.g., a d.rule: When a document names a piece (e.g., a dresser) at a specific location and the nearest valid placement is more than 1 m away, the fit stage must either (a) relax the placement constraint to allow the piece at the named location if it does not clash, or (b) flag the discrepancy for the architect rather than silently dropping the piece.

an opening in the outer wall that is ful.rule: An opening in the outer wall that is fully or mostly blocked by furniture and has no passage function should be read as a window, not a door. The reading stage must check whether the opening is a passage or a window based on its clear width and the furniture in its approach.

an outer-wall opening whose approach is.rule: An outer-wall opening whose approach is blocked by drawn furniture and that has no swing arc is a window, not a door; the reading must classify it by its sill and the furniture in front of it, not by its width.

a movable sanitary piece (washbasin) tha.rule: A movable sanitary piece (washbasin) that overlaps a fixed drawn piece (bathtub) must be repositioned to clear it; the fit stage must resolve the clash by moving the movable piece, not the fixed one.

a furniture piece that covers a window b.rule: A furniture piece that covers a window blocks light and ventilation and must be moved to clear the opening; the fit stage must keep furniture off window sills.

the big loop must run enough cycles to r.rule: The big loop must run enough cycles to raise the house score; a single cycle that hits the deadline without improving the score is a process failure that requires more cycles.

views marked for review by the check sta.rule: Views marked for review by the check stage must be addressed by the agent in the next round; the agent must re-frame or remove cameras that fail the review.

when the agent's swap_model attempts for.rule: When the agent's swap_model attempts for a washbasin are all refused by fit rules (caps, height), the code must allow at least one model from the piece's allowed list that passes the fit rules, or the agent must be given a different tool (e.g. resize_piece) to adjust the piece to fit a better model.

When the agent's swap_model attempts for a washbasin are all refused by fit rules (caps, height, sloped ceiling), the code must allow at least one model from the piece's allowed list that passes the fit rules, or the agent must be given a different tool (e.g. resize_piece) to adjust the piece to fit a better model.

a drawn floor lamp that blocks the free.rule: A drawn floor lamp that blocks the free zone in front of a drawn armchair must be repositioned by the fit stage; the drawn_lock constraint (0.3 m max move) must not prevent resolving a physical clash between two drawn pieces.

when the agent's relayout_room attempts.rule: When the agent's relayout_room attempts for a large living room are refused because they do not resolve a walkway constraint (G11), the code must allow the relayout to proceed if the walkway constraint is satisfied by the new layout, or the agent must be given a tool to adjust the door positions.

when a drawn wardrobe is not built becau.rule: When a drawn wardrobe is not built because its cluster is larger than 4.5 m on a side, the code must either build the wardrobe as a separate piece or allow the cluster to be split; the 'not built' reason must not hide a loss of a drawn element.

a camera in a small room (dressing room).rule: A camera in a small room (dressing room) must be positioned to show the room's main function and furniture, not pressed against a wall framing only a door and a sliver of a wardrobe.

outdoor furniture on a terrace or balcon.rule: Outdoor furniture on a terrace or balcony must be a coherent set (matching style, material, and design concept), not a random assortment of mismatched pieces.

interior renders must include the room's.rule: Interior renders must include the room's lighting and material styling layers; a bare grey-box render of a furnished room is a failure of the render stage, not the model.

bathroom renders must include warm ambie.rule: Bathroom renders must include warm ambient lighting and styled surfaces to match the project's reference aesthetic; a sterile white box is unacceptable.

interior camera views must frame all key.rule: Interior camera views must frame all key fixtures of the room without cutting them off at the frame edges.

kitchen renders must convey a warm, live.rule: Kitchen renders must convey a warm, lived-in feel with styled surfaces, plants, and warm lighting; a sterile box with mismatched furniture is a render and styling failure.

kitchen rooms must include decorative el.rule: Kitchen rooms must include decorative elements (plants, wall art, counter decor) and warm lighting to create a cozy atmosphere; a bare kitchen is a styling failure.

dining chairs must match the style and c.rule: Dining chairs must match the style and color of the dining table and the room's overall aesthetic; a single mismatched chair is a fit failure.

kitchen renders must convey a warm, text.rule: Kitchen renders must convey a warm, textured, lived-in feel; a sterile box with boxy mismatched furniture is a render and styling failure.

kitchen appliances must match the style.rule: Kitchen appliances must match the style and finish of the cabinetry and the room's overall aesthetic; a glossy black fridge in a matte rustic-white kitchen is a fit failure.

dining tables must match the style and c.rule: Dining tables must match the style and color of the room's overall aesthetic; a round wooden table in a stark minimalist white kitchen is a fit failure.

kitchen renders must convey a warm, text.rule: Kitchen renders must convey a warm, textured, lived-in feel with coherent furniture; a grey box with sparse blocky furniture is a render and styling failure.

living rooms must include wall art or mi.rule: Living rooms must include wall art or mirrors to anchor the space; large empty walls are a styling failure.

dining tables must include decorative el.rule: Dining tables must include decorative elements (centerpiece, runner, bowl of fruit) to look styled; a bare table is a styling failure.

living room sofas must form a cohesive p.rule: Living room sofas must form a cohesive palette and style; a rust-colored leather sofa clashing with a white sofa and red egg chair is a fit failure.

living room renders must convey a mid-ce.rule: Living room renders must convey a mid-century aesthetic with cohesive furniture and styling layers; a flat beige box with mismatched furniture is a render and styling failure.

living room sofas must form a cohesive p.rule: Living room sofas must form a cohesive palette and style; a plain beige sofa clashing with a rust-orange sofa is a fit failure.

living room seating areas must include w.rule: Living room seating areas must include wall art or mirrors to anchor the space; a large blank wall is a styling failure.

interior renders of wet rooms must inclu.rule: Interior renders of wet rooms must include warm accent lighting and styled surfaces (textiles, wood, accessories) to avoid a sterile, unfinished appearance.

bathroom scenes must include at least on.rule: Bathroom scenes must include at least one warm light source (e.g., pendant, sconce) to create a cozy atmosphere, not just flat daylight.

when a fixture is under a sloped ceiling.rule: When a fixture is under a sloped ceiling and all standard library models are refused for height, the fitting stage should prioritize low-profile or wall-hung models that fit the clearance, or flag the geometry for review rather than leaving a crude placeholder.

camera views of bathrooms must frame the.rule: Camera views of bathrooms must frame the main functional group (vanity, toilet, shower) and include styling elements to avoid a 'grey box' appearance.

furniture in a children's room must be s.rule: Furniture in a children's room must be stylistically coherent and finished; raw slabs and mismatched office chairs are not acceptable.

wardrobe models must have visible doors,.rule: Wardrobe models must have visible doors, handles, and depth to read as functional furniture, not flat slabs.

desk models must have finished surfaces.rule: Desk models must have finished surfaces and legs that match the room's style (e.g., light wood for Scandinavian).

office chairs in bedrooms/children's roo.rule: Office chairs in bedrooms/children's rooms should be light-colored and stylistically appropriate, not dark glossy plastic.

children's room renders must show a cohe.rule: Children's room renders must show a coherent, stylish furniture set, not a mismatched office corner.

furniture in a single room must be from.rule: Furniture in a single room must be from a coherent design family to avoid a chaotic, mismatched appearance.

when a room has multiple beds, they must.rule: When a room has multiple beds, they must be from the same design family or style to appear as a matching set.

bathroom camera views must frame the mai.rule: Bathroom camera views must frame the main functional group (shower, toilet, washbasin) to show the room's layout and styling.

camera views must include the main fixtu.rule: Camera views must include the main fixtures of the room to avoid a 'bare corner' appearance.

bathroom scenes must include styled surf.rule: Bathroom scenes must include styled surfaces and accessories to avoid a bare, empty appearance.

bedroom renders must show the full furni.rule: Bedroom renders must show the full furniture set and styling layers to avoid a bare, unfinished appearance.

bedroom scenes must include layered, coz.rule: Bedroom scenes must include layered, cozy styling (throws, cushions, rugs) to avoid a flat, bare appearance.

when a bedroom wall carries two full-hei.rule: When a bedroom wall carries two full-height door openings side by side, the reading must not build both as doors: it must check the plan for a window, a built-in closet opening, or a wall line and resolve the second opening accordingly before the model stage.

the exterior site must carry the referen.rule: The exterior site must carry the reference's planting and hardscape (hedges, trees, a path to the entrance) so the facade is not a bare white box.

the entrance must read as a designed thr.rule: The entrance must read as a designed threshold: a path and a front court (and seating where the reference shows it) rather than a bare slab door.

a decor cushion that penetrates its host.rule: A decor cushion that penetrates its host by more than 0.03 m must be re-seated on the host's top surface (or dropped) rather than left unbuilt; the rest check should nudge the cushion up to the host's seat plane instead of refusing it.

a desk in a bedroom must be placed near.rule: A desk in a bedroom must be placed near the window for natural light and within reach of the bed, not in the middle of a wall creating a dead zone.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece's footprint is a detail of that piece and must not be built as a separate piece, even if an AI pass names it a type that fits its size; the reading stage should suppress it as a detail.

the reading stage must read attdef entit.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF entities (attribute definitions) in DWG files; 28 ATTDEF entities were not read, which may hold room labels, dimensions or other data the ledger checks.

site decor read outside the walls of l1.rule: Site decor read outside the walls of L1 (the upper floor) must be mapped to L0 (the ground floor, where the site is) and used in the site build; 35 decor items were read but not used, 20 of them repeating the ground plan's symbols at the same place.

when a room outline holds two labels (e..rule: When a room outline holds two labels (e.g. 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ'), the reading stage must split the room into two (living and dining) rather than keeping one room with a second label; the split should use the second label's anchor and area.

every printed area label on a plan must.rule: Every printed area label on a plan must be bound to the room outline it sits in and stored on that room's record; an unbound area label is a lost check, not a warning.

when the reading selects a wall layer by.rule: When the reading selects a wall layer by evidence and documents the primitives it excluded, that is a correct, auditable decision, not a lost element.

decor symbols read on an upper floor tha.rule: Decor symbols read on an upper floor that duplicate the ground floor's site symbols at the same coordinates are a known artifact (site.decor_other_levels) and are correctly excluded from the model.

any layer whose name indicates a buildin.rule: Any layer whose name indicates a building element (e.g. DENIZLIK = bathtub/basin, DUVAR = wall, PENCERE = window) must be either used by the model or explicitly named in a warning with the reason it was excluded; a silent, unused named layer is a loss.

a piece placed by the decor stage and dr.rule: A piece placed by the decor stage and dropped by the agent stage is a loss; the agent's next round must restore or re-place it.

a dining table in a living/dining room s.rule: A dining table in a living/dining room should have at least a tablecloth or a simple setting; a bare table is an incomplete decor.

armchairs in a bedroom should match the.rule: Armchairs in a bedroom should match the room's palette and style; a mismatched set (e.g. modern plastic in a warm, neutral room) is a decor error.

a piece listed in a room's data must be.rule: A piece listed in a room's data must be placed and visible in the render; a listed-but-invisible piece is a loss.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading must either split the outline into two rooms or assign the extra label to a separate room; a single outline with two labels is a misread.

a kitchen counter must be built with vis.rule: A kitchen counter must be built with visible appliances and a proper layout; a bare box without appliances is a placeholder, not a kitchen.

a desk and chair in a children's room sh.rule: A desk and chair in a children's room should be sized and styled for a child; a large, formal office setup is a mismatch.

a chair that differs from its drawn plac.rule: A chair that differs from its drawn place by more than the tolerance (0.05 m) must be swapped for a model that fits its drawn position.

a dresser that differs from its drawn pl.rule: A dresser that differs from its drawn place by more than the tolerance (0.05 m) must be swapped for a model that fits its drawn position.

a small (<= 4 m2) hall/entry room that h.rule: A small (<= 4 m2) hall/entry room that holds a shoe cabinet is a plausible entrance storage nook; the type 'hall' is correct and no change is needed.

a hall containing a shoe cabinet and a s.rule: A hall containing a shoe cabinet and a stair is a plausible entrance hall; no change is needed.

a bathroom containing a shower, toilet a.rule: A bathroom containing a shower, toilet and washbasin is a plausible bathroom; no change is needed.

a bathroom containing a bathtub, toilet,.rule: A bathroom containing a bathtub, toilet, washbasin and washing machine is a plausible bathroom; no change is needed.

a bedroom containing a single bed, dress.rule: A bedroom containing a single bed, dresser, nightstand and wardrobe is a plausible bedroom; no change is needed.

a bedroom containing a double bed, desk,.rule: A bedroom containing a double bed, desk, dresser, nightstand, office chair and wardrobe is a plausible bedroom; no change is needed.

a bedroom containing an armchair, double.rule: A bedroom containing an armchair, double bed, desk, floor lamp, nightstand and office chair is a plausible bedroom; no change is needed.

a living room containing an armchair, bo.rule: A living room containing an armchair, bookshelf, chair, floor lamp, potted plant, sofa, coffee table and dining table is a plausible living room; no change is needed.

a kitchen containing a chair, fridge, co.rule: A kitchen containing a chair, fridge, counter, sink, stair, stove, dining table and wall cabinet is a plausible kitchen; no change is needed.

a small hall with no pieces is a plausib.rule: A small hall with no pieces is a plausible hall; no change is needed.

a bathroom containing a bathtub, toilet.rule: A bathroom containing a bathtub, toilet and washbasin is a plausible bathroom; no change is needed.

a fitter must not place a piece so that.rule: A fitter must not place a piece so that the ray from an opening hits it (the piece covers the window's clear zone); the piece must be moved clear of the opening's clear zone.

when an elevation's openings are to be c.rule: When an elevation's openings are to be checked against the plans, the reading must record the elevation's side (from the north arrow or a labelled side); if no side can be determined, the check is skipped and the elevation is flagged as 'side unknown' rather than silently left unchecked.

when a drawn section is to be checked po.rule: When a drawn section is to be checked point-by-point against the roof, the reading must verify that the section line runs one-to-one with the plan (its ends within 0.30 m of the roof outline's ends along the section axis); if not, the check is skipped and the section is flagged as 'not aligned with plan' rather than silently left unchecked.
when a drawn section is to be checked po.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

when an elevation is to be compared with.rule: When an elevation is to be compared with the model, the reading must record the elevation's view bearing or side; if neither can be determined, the comparison is skipped and the elevation is flagged as 'bearing unknown' rather than silently left uncomparable.

when a drawn dining group's anchor (tabl.rule: When a drawn dining group's anchor (table) is locked by the drawing and the solver finds no free span that fits the full group, it must stop after the first failed span and report the group as 'drawn-locked, no free span' instead of retrying the same locked anchor on other spans until max_tries; the drawn anchor is the cause, not the span.

the fitting stage must not fall back to.rule: The fitting stage must not fall back to a parametric mesh for a wall_cabinet when a library model of the correct type and size exists; it must search the library for a wall_cabinet model that fits the drawn footprint before using parametric.

the fitting stage must not refuse a gene.rule: The fitting stage must not refuse a generated model when it is the only model of the correct type that fits the drawn footprint; it must accept the generated model and flag it for review rather than leaving the piece with a placeholder-looking model.

when the reading records the same openin.rule: When the reading records the same opening twice (same span, same width), the build stage merges them into one element and the conservation check must treat the duplicate record as resolved, not as a loss.

axis bubbles, level marks, and other dra.rule: Axis bubbles, level marks, and other drawing annotations on layers like 'AKS YAZI' or 'AKS' are never built; the conservation check should not flag them as lost elements.

small drawn shapes (under 0.30 m) that l.rule: Small drawn shapes (under 0.30 m) that lie entirely inside a larger piece's footprint are treated as cushions or details of that piece, not as independent furniture to be built.

when a library model for a piece include.rule: When a library model for a piece includes built-in cushions or pillows, separately drawn cushion elements on that piece are not built as independent objects.

decor or detail elements that depend on.rule: Decor or detail elements that depend on a host piece are only built if the host piece is built; if the host is not built, the decor is correctly omitted.

axis bubbles on layers like 'aks' are dr.rule: Axis bubbles on layers like 'AKS' are drawing annotations and are never built.

structural columns that support a verand.rule: Structural columns that support a veranda or balcony are built as part of that structure's posts, not as separate column elements.

level marks on layers like 'kot' are dra.rule: Level marks on layers like 'kot' are drawing annotations and are never built as physical elements.

site area labels (veranda, balcony) are.rule: Site area labels (veranda, balcony) are represented by the ground/paving surfaces in the site model, not as separate built elements.

when two drawn outlines represent the sa.rule: When two drawn outlines represent the same physical object (one inside the other, same type), the build stage merges them into one element.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece of the same type is treated as a duplicate or part of the larger piece, not as an independent element.

when a kitchen run is drawn as a single.rule: When a kitchen run is drawn as a single outline containing its fixtures (sink, stove, etc.), the build stage decomposes it into individual counter segments and fixtures rather than building the outline as one piece.

a drawn outline that surrounds 3 or more.rule: A drawn outline that surrounds 3 or more other pieces and is larger than any single piece is treated as a rug or zone outline, not as furniture.

small drawn shapes (under 0.30 m) that l.rule: Small drawn shapes (under 0.30 m) that lie entirely inside a sofa's footprint are treated as cushions or details, not as independent furniture.

when a piece is removed by an ai decisio.rule: When a piece is removed by an AI decision (AI.remove_piece) but the drawing clearly shows it as a distinct, correctly-typed piece in a room that allows that type, the build stage should not drop it; the removal decision should be reviewed.

a conservation finding whose 'not built'.rule: A conservation finding whose 'not built' reason is 'the answer to AI.remove_piece:<id>' is a false alarm: the removal was a deliberate decision, not a stage dropping a drawn element.

an untyped drawn mark that is a long thi.rule: An untyped drawn mark that is a long thin cluster (>4.5 m on one side, <0.7 m on the other) in a bedroom is a dimension line or outline fragment, not furniture; the build stage may refuse it without a loss.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m that fit.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m that fits no furniture type is a detail line (threshold, valve, shelf edge), not a buildable piece; the build stage may refuse it without a loss.

a drawn mark that is 60% or more contain.rule: A drawn mark that is 60% or more contained within another built piece is a detail of that piece, not a separate furniture item; the build stage may refuse it without a loss.

when a nightstand is not built because i.rule: When a nightstand is not built because it overlaps a bed and no free place is within 1.0 m, the furniture agent must re-solve the bedroom layout (relayout_room or place_group) to find a valid position for the nightstand.

a stair piece on the top floor that 'arr.rule: A stair piece on the top floor that 'arrives from' the floor below and has 'no level above' is correctly not built again; it is the same physical stair, not a new one.

a decoration that is 'not built: its hos.rule: A decoration that is 'not built: its host <id> is not built' is a false alarm when the host was removed by an explicit AI decision; the decoration is correctly absent.
A decoration that is 'not built: its host <id> is not built' is a real loss when the host is a standard furniture piece that should be built; fix the host first.

when a furniture name text is found in a.rule: When a furniture name text is found in a room that already contains a piece of that type, the text is considered satisfied and no new piece is added.

when a furniture name text names a piece.rule: When a furniture name text names a piece type not present in the room, and the room's area is sufficient, the solver should place the piece at the text's location or the nearest valid spot, even if it is more than 1 m from the text, as long as it is within the room and clear of doors and other pieces.

an outer-wall opening whose approach is.rule: An outer-wall opening whose approach is blocked by a drawn piece and that has no outside destination is a window, not a door.

a hall under 3 m2 is a passage and needs.rule: A hall under 3 m2 is a passage and needs no furniture.

a drawn piece that overlaps a drawn fixt.rule: A drawn piece that overlaps a drawn fixture in a wet room is moved to the nearest free place, clear of the fixture and the window.

a drawn piece that covers a window is mo.rule: A drawn piece that covers a window is moved to the nearest free place, clear of the window.

a labelled outdoor site area (veranda, t.rule: A labelled outdoor site area (veranda, terrace, balcony) that is drawn in the plan must be built as a platform with its drawn outline, even if it is not a room.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcon.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a platform with its own floor and railing, not dropped as 'no outline'.

a room typed as a dressing room (soyunma.rule: A room typed as a dressing room (soyunma odası) must be furnished with its dressing set (bench, mirror, storage) so its purpose is legible; a bare wardrobe is not a dressing room.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group, not a wall or door leaf; if the only furniture is a wardrobe, the view must show it.
An interior camera must frame the room's contents (here the shoe cabinet and doors), not a bare wall corner.

a scene check failure on a level is a bu.rule: A scene check failure on a level is a build-stage defect; re-run the build for that level to re-fit the offending pieces.

a dresser that floats or intersects a wa.rule: A dresser that floats or intersects a wall/window is a bad model fit; swap to a model whose depth clears the wall and whose front faces the room.

a planned piece that is missing from the.rule: A planned piece that is missing from the scene is a build loss; retype it to force a rebuild with a suitable model.

an exterior view that must show a window.rule: An exterior view that must show a window must frame it; if the window is not in the frame, re-aim the camera at it.

strokes on the furniture layer inside a.rule: Strokes on the furniture layer inside a room that no piece uses must be read as furniture (a sofa, chairs around a table) and built, not dropped.

a second label inside a room outline (e..rule: A second label inside a room outline (e.g. 'ANTRE') is a separate room the reading must split out, not a duplicate label of the same room.

a named piece in the documents (e.g. '*s.rule: A named piece in the documents (e.g. '*SIFONIYER' = dresser) that the model lacks must be added at its named location.

a piece removed by ai that is a valid pi.rule: A piece removed by AI that is a valid piece in its room must be rebuilt; retyping it forces a rebuild with a suitable model.

a drawn cluster wider than 4.5 m that is.rule: A drawn cluster wider than 4.5 m that is not a single furniture type is a built-in or architectural element (e.g. a long low bench, window seat, or storage run); the build stage must model it as a built-in module rather than dropping it as 'not furniture', and the mark_not_furniture tool must not be used for a drawn element that the documents show as a functional part of the room.

site areas labeled in the documents (e.g.rule: Site areas labeled in the documents (e.g. VERANDA, BALKON) must be built as structural outlines with floors and railings when they are primary outdoor living spaces; the site stage must not skip them as 'no outline' when the documents clearly label them.

a children's room (çocuk odası) whose dr.rule: A children's room (Çocuk Odası) whose drawn anchor is a double bed is a misread: the room's function is two sleepers, so the anchor is a bunk bed (or loft bed), not a single double bed.

a hall's anchor piece (shoe cabinet) tha.rule: A hall's anchor piece (shoe cabinet) that is 'not built' leaves the room empty in the render; the anchor must be built with a real model, not left parametric or absent.

a bathtub and a washbasin that overlap w.rule: A bathtub and a washbasin that overlap with no free place within the move limits means the bathroom set was placed without checking the wet-room clearance; the set must be re-solved as a unit so the basin clears the tub.

a window whose sightline is blocked by f.rule: A window whose sightline is blocked by furniture means the furniture was placed without checking the window clearance; the piece must be moved or the window re-placed so the view through is clear.

a kitchen counter built with its top at.rule: A kitchen counter built with its top at 2.10 m over the floor is a misread size: the counter's working height is 0.90-0.97 m, so the piece must be resized to a real counter height.

a washbasin placed at the level of the b.rule: A washbasin placed at the level of the bathtub rim is a misread height: the basin's rim must be at 0.85 m working height, not at tub-rim level.

a dresser that renders as a floating whi.rule: A dresser that renders as a floating white railing is a wrong model: the model does not match the piece's type, so it must be swapped to a real dresser model.

an entrance with a handrail that does no.rule: An entrance with a handrail that does not connect to the steps and a floating canopy is a broken entrance: the entrance solution must be set so the steps, handrail and canopy are built as a coherent unit.

a room typed 'other' that contains only.rule: A room typed 'other' that contains only a wardrobe is a misread type: a room with a wardrobe and no other fixtures is a storage/dressing room, not 'other'.

a dresser named in the documents (text).rule: A dresser named in the documents (TEXT) that cannot be placed because the nearest valid spot is more than 1 m from the text is a fit failure: the fit stage must place the piece at the text's location even if it is not the nearest valid spot, or the text's location must be checked against the room's walls and doors before the fit stage runs.

a 2.15 m sliding door read from its line.rule: A 2.15 m sliding door read from its lines (no swing arc) in the outer wall of a living room, with a drawn piece standing across its approach, is a misread: it is a window at the floor's sill, not a door.

a window in a wet room with furniture pl.rule: A window in a wet room with furniture placed in front of it is not a passage blockage; the furniture placement is a fit issue, not a reading error.

a window in a kitchen with a counter pla.rule: A window in a kitchen with a counter placed in front of it is not a passage blockage; the furniture placement is a fit issue, not a reading error.

a window in a living room with furniture.rule: A window in a living room with furniture placed in front of it is not a passage blockage; the furniture placement is a fit issue, not a reading error.

a window in a bedroom with furniture pla.rule: A window in a bedroom with furniture placed in front of it is not a passage blockage; the furniture placement is a fit issue, not a reading error.
