a window in a hall with furniture placed.rule: A window in a hall with furniture placed in front of it is not a passage blockage; the furniture placement is a fit issue, not a reading error.

furniture pieces in a bathroom must not.rule: Furniture pieces in a bathroom must not overlap; the washbasin should be placed clear of the bathtub.

furniture pieces must not cover windows;.rule: Furniture pieces must not cover windows; they should be placed clear of the window to allow light and ventilation.

the big loop should run for at least 2 c.rule: The big loop should run for at least 2 cycles to allow the agent to improve the house score, unless the deadline is reached.

views marked for review should be adjust.rule: Views marked for review should be adjusted to show the room's key features and avoid showing bare walls or cluttered corners.

outdoor areas should be furnished with a.rule: Outdoor areas should be furnished with appropriate outdoor furniture (e.g., seating, tables, plants) to match the project's style and reference.

bathroom renders should include styled s.rule: Bathroom renders should include styled surfaces (e.g., warm wood, stone) and the washbasin should be placed at a logical height (e.g., wall-hung at 0.85 m).

bathroom walls should be clad with natur.rule: Bathroom walls should be clad with natural materials (e.g., warm wood, stone) to match the project's style and reference.

a kitchen render must show a styled dini.rule: A kitchen render must show a styled dining set, wall art, and warm lighting; blocky primitive models and bare walls are a failure of the styling stage, not the geometry.

every habitable room in a styled project.rule: Every habitable room in a styled project must have at least one wall art piece; bare walls are a missing decor layer.

a kitchen render must show a complete, s.rule: A kitchen render must show a complete, styled kitchen with wall cabinets, a cohesive dining set, and warm lighting; blocky primitives and bare counters are a styling failure.

furniture models must match the project'.rule: Furniture models must match the project's style (Scandinavian: wood, woven light, art, styled surfaces); blocky primitives are a model-selection failure.

a dining table model must match the proj.rule: A dining table model must match the project's style (Scandinavian/minimal); a simple oval slab that clashes with the light, airy style is a model-selection failure.

a living room render must show a cohesiv.rule: A living room render must show a cohesive furniture palette and decor layers (art, lighting, textiles); a chaotic mix of clashing styles is a styling failure.

an armchair model must match the project.rule: An armchair model must match the project's style (Scandinavian/minimal); a loud 1960s design piece that clashes with the neutral palette is a model-selection failure.

a sofa model must match the project's st.rule: A sofa model must match the project's style (Scandinavian/modern); an orange leather sofa that clashes with the grey sofa and other chairs is a model-selection failure.

a living room's central seating area mus.rule: A living room's central seating area must have a coffee table as an anchor and styled surface; an empty central area is a missing functional piece.

a living room render must show a cohesiv.rule: A living room render must show a cohesive furniture palette and decor layers; a bare, unfinished shell with mismatched models is a styling failure.

a sofa model must match the project's st.rule: A sofa model must match the project's style (Scandinavian/modern); a dated, bulky model that clashes with the modern, light style is a model-selection failure.

a living room render must show a cohesiv.rule: A living room render must show a cohesive furniture palette; a mismatched collection of styles (rust leather, red egg chair, white sofa, glass dining) is a styling failure.

a bathroom render must show a cohesive,.rule: A bathroom render must show a cohesive, styled space with warm lighting and textured surfaces; a floating black washbasin and flat, cold light are a styling failure.

a washbasin model must match the project.rule: A washbasin model must match the project's style (minimal/scandinavian) and the room's palette (white); a floating, boxy black placeholder is a model-selection failure.

a bathroom render must show warm, inviti.rule: A bathroom render must show warm, inviting lighting; flat, cold, clinical light is a lighting failure.

a bedroom render must show a coherent sp.rule: A bedroom render must show a coherent spatial arrangement; floating, overlapping, or impossible furniture placement is a layout failure.

a bedroom sized for one sleeper (under ~.rule: A bedroom sized for one sleeper (under ~25 m2 without a second drawn bed) is furnished with a single bed; a second full bed is only built when the drawing shows two beds or the room is a twin/dormitory.

every room with a large window or balcon.rule: Every room with a large window or balcony door gets a softening layer (curtains or blinds) in the furnishing pass; bare glazing is a missing layer, not a finished look.

an interior camera must be placed at a f.rule: An interior camera must be placed at a free point that shows the room's main pieces and is not blocked by a railing, partition or furniture edge; a view whose foreground is a structural element that hides the room is a bad camera, not a bad room.

a bed model whose mattress is a flat box.rule: A bed model whose mattress is a flat box and whose throw is an untextured decal is a crude placeholder; the furniture agent must pick a model with a real mattress, frame and bedding that matches the project's style.

a room typed as a children's room is fur.rule: A room typed as a children's room is furnished with age-appropriate, playful, layered pieces (bed, desk, storage, rug, plants, art) in the project's style; a generic adult bedroom set is a style mismatch, not a valid furnishing.

a bathroom camera must be placed at a fr.rule: A bathroom camera must be placed at a free point that shows the room's main fixtures (shower, basin, toilet) and is not pressed against a wall or partition; a close-up of a corner that hides the fixtures is a bad camera.

a room whose reference style is defined.rule: A room whose reference style is defined by abundant greenery gets multiple plants (hanging, floor, windowsill) in the furnishing pass; a single low-poly plant is a missing layer, not a finished look.

furniture in one room must share a cohes.rule: Furniture in one room must share a cohesive style; a mid-century modern armchair that clashes with the room's rustic pine and modern grey pieces is a style mismatch that the furniture agent must resolve by swapping to a model that fits the room's set.

a nightstand and its lamp must match the.rule: A nightstand and its lamp must match the room's style; a rustic pine nightstand with a harsh modern lamp that clashes with the bed and chairs is a style mismatch that the furniture agent must resolve by swapping to a model that fits the room's set.

a hall camera must be placed at a free p.rule: A hall camera must be placed at a free point that shows the room's anchor pieces (shoe cabinet, mirror, art) and is not a bare stair landing; a view that reads as a construction site is a bad camera or a missing furnishing layer.

a hall/entrance room gets an anchor piec.rule: A hall/entrance room gets an anchor piece (shoe cabinet, console, mirror) and at least one styling layer (art, lighting, warm material) in the furnishing pass; a bare hall is a missing layer, not a finished look.

a hall camera must be placed at a free p.rule: A hall camera must be placed at a free point that shows the room's doors and anchor pieces; a close-up of a wall corner and louvered panel that hides the hall is a bad camera.

a bedroom whose reference shows a textur.rule: A bedroom whose reference shows a textured rug gets a rug with real texture in the furnishing pass; a flat, untextured mat is a missing layer, not a finished look.

a bedroom must be furnished with warm, l.rule: A bedroom must be furnished with warm, layered, organic materials (plants, textiles, art, warm light) in the project's style; a 'grey box' with a bed and flat untextured surfaces is a missing styling layer, not a finished look.

a dressing room camera must be placed at.rule: A dressing room camera must be placed at a free point that shows the room's main group (wardrobe, mirror, seating) and is not pressed against furniture; a tight close-up of a door and wardrobe edge is a bad camera.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's furniture, never a bare wall or door frame; if the room is too small to show its pieces, the view is removed rather than left on a wall.

exterior presentation views must be rend.rule: Exterior presentation views must be rendered with the facade's material palette (cladding, frames, roof) and the site's landscaping and lighting applied; a grey-box massing study is not an acceptable client exterior.

the facade material slot must carry the.rule: The facade material slot must carry the project's cladding look (wood/stone) so the exterior is not a flat untextured box.

the site must carry landscaping (trees,.rule: The site must carry landscaping (trees, hedge, planters) so the exterior is not a flat empty green plane.

a decor cushion that cannot rest on its.rule: A decor cushion that cannot rest on its host without penetration is correctly left unbuilt; it is a minor cosmetic item, not a lost piece.

a bed model whose bedding renders as a m.rule: A bed model whose bedding renders as a mess (askew pillows, crumpled throw) should be swapped for a model with cleaner bedding geometry.

a drawn piece that is 60%+ inside anothe.rule: A drawn piece that is 60%+ inside another piece but whose size and AI naming fit a distinct furniture type (e.g. a 0.40 m floor lamp beside a bed) is a lost piece, not a detail of the host.

the dwg reader must parse attdef (attrib.rule: The DWG reader must parse ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities in addition to TEXT and MTEXT, so that block attributes (room labels, dimensions, notes) are not silently dropped.

site decor read on an upper level (l1) t.rule: Site decor read on an upper level (L1) that duplicates the ground-floor (L0) symbols at the same location is a reading artefact and should be discarded, not carried into the site model.

when a room outline holds two room label.rule: When a room outline holds two room labels, the reading must split the outline at the wall between them so each label becomes its own room, instead of keeping the larger label and dropping the other.

every printed area label on a plan must.rule: Every printed area label on a plan must be bound to its room so the area check can run; an unbound label is a lost check.

a reading warning that records the evide.rule: A reading warning that records the evidence for a chosen wall layer and the count of primitives left out is an informational note, not a lost element.

decor symbols read on an upper level tha.rule: Decor symbols read on an upper level that duplicate the ground plan's symbols at the same place are not used, because the site belongs to the ground floor.

a drawing layer whose name denotes a san.rule: A drawing layer whose name denotes a sanitary fixture (e.g. DENIZLIK = bidet) must be read as that fixture and placed in the matching wet room, not left unused and unnamed.

a piece placed by the decor stage must n.rule: A piece placed by the decor stage must not be dropped by the agent stage; if the agent removes it, its next round must restore or re-place it.

a dining table in a furnished home shoul.rule: A dining table in a furnished home should be styled (setting, cloth or props) so the surface is not bare in the render.

furniture in a room must match the room'.rule: Furniture in a room must match the room's palette and style; a mismatched set should be swapped for a model that fits.

a piece listed in a room's data must be.rule: A piece listed in a room's data must be visible in the room's render; if it is not, the agent must place or re-place it so it shows.

a drawn piece must be built within the d.rule: A drawn piece must be built within the drawing tolerance of its drawn place; a layout offset beyond tolerance must be corrected.

every elevation sheet must carry a north.rule: Every elevation sheet must carry a north arrow or a side label; if the drawing lacks one, the reading stage must infer the side from the plan's section cut line and record it, so the elevation-to-plan opening check can run.

a section is only comparable to the plan.rule: A section is only comparable to the plan/roof when its cut line matches the plan outline within 0.30 m at both ends and its roof line is monotonic; if not, the reading stage must flag the section as non-comparable and skip the point-by-point check instead of forcing it.
a section is only comparable to the plan.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

every elevation must be assigned a view.rule: Every elevation must be assigned a view bearing or side at reading time (from its north arrow, side label, or the plan's section cut line); if none can be determined, the elevation is marked non-comparable and excluded from the model comparison rather than silently skipped.

a parametric opening built in the style'.rule: A parametric opening built in the style's finish when no library model of the building's window family fits the drawn size is a correct fallback, not a defect: it keeps one door and window language and the opening is present.

when a drawn kitchen fitting is built as.rule: When a drawn kitchen fitting is built as a parametric mesh below the library level, swap it to a library model of the same type and matching footprint so it renders at library quality.

the library must carry at least one wall.rule: The library must carry at least one wall_cabinet model per common kitchen footprint (e.g. 0.90 x 0.35 m) so a drawn wall cabinet is never forced to a parametric mesh below the library level.
The library must carry at least one wall_cabinet model per common kitchen footprint (e.g. 0.59 x 0.35 m) so a drawn wall cabinet is never forced to a parametric mesh below the library level.

a kitchen worktop and backsplash must ca.rule: A kitchen worktop and backsplash must carry a textured material (stone, wood or tile) rather than a flat untextured surface, so the kitchen does not read as a grey box.

a dining table model must match the room.rule: A dining table model must match the room's stated style (here modern/minimal); an ornate, textured-base table is a style mismatch and should be swapped for a minimal/modern model of the same footprint.

a statement armchair must fit the room's.rule: A statement armchair must fit the room's cohesive style; a bold, dated piece (e.g. a red egg chair) in a modern/minimal room is a style mismatch and should be swapped for a minimal/modern model of the same footprint.

large interior windows should carry a si.rule: Large interior windows should carry a simple curtain or soft layer by default so they do not read as bare glass in renders; the scene stage should add a curtain layer to large openings unless the style is explicitly bare.

a wardrobe model must match the room's w.rule: A wardrobe model must match the room's warm wood tones; a flat white generic unit is a style mismatch and should be swapped for a minimal/modern or scandinavian model of the same footprint.

a bed model must include layered bedding.rule: A bed model must include layered bedding (duvet, throw, textured pillows) rather than a single flat sheet, so the bedroom reads as styled, not clinical.

two armchairs in the same room must shar.rule: Two armchairs in the same room must share a style family; a mismatched grey quilted chair next to a white chair is a set mismatch and should be swapped for a model in the same minimal/modern/scandinavian family.

a wardrobe model must be a designed piec.rule: A wardrobe model must be a designed piece, not a massive flat block; swap a placeholder block for a scandinavian/rustic model of a comparable footprint.

a single bed model must include textured.rule: A single bed model must include textured bedding (cushions, throws) rather than plain white, so the bedroom reads as inviting.

a front door must carry a styled materia.rule: A front door must carry a styled material and detail (e.g. a rich wood or a modern panel) rather than a flat placeholder slab, so it reads as a focal point of the facade.

an exterior path should carry bollard or.rule: An exterior path should carry bollard or path lighting by default so it does not read as a bare, unlit concrete strip in night or dusk renders; the scene stage should add path lighting to the main walkway.

door symbols on the 'kapi' layer that ar.rule: Door symbols on the 'KAPI' layer that are not assigned to a built door ID (d_L*) and are not required for circulation or access are treated as decorative or redundant symbols and are not built.

hatch patterns and 2d drafting symbols o.rule: Hatch patterns and 2D drafting symbols on layers like 'TARAMA' are annotations and are not converted to 3D geometry.

details of outdoor spaces (steps, edges).rule: Details of outdoor spaces (steps, edges) are considered built if they are part of a larger built structure (like a veranda), even if the site area outline is missing.

coordinate system offsets between the dr.rule: Coordinate system offsets between the drawing sheet and the model origin are informational and do not require correction if the model is internally consistent.

discrepancies between structural levels.rule: Discrepancies between structural levels and finished floor levels in drawings are handled by the reading stage and are informational if the model uses the correct FFL.

level marks and similar symbols are clas.rule: Level marks and similar symbols are classified as symbols, not furniture, and are not built as 3D objects.

text labels in drawings that match exist.rule: Text labels in drawings that match existing pieces in the model are confirmations, not errors.

text labels for furniture that cannot be.rule: Text labels for furniture that cannot be placed due to space constraints are informational and are handled by the placement stage.

zone labels in drawings that match exist.rule: Zone labels in drawings that match existing furniture in the model are confirmations, not errors.

pieces typed by context (e.g., near a ta.rule: Pieces typed by context (e.g., near a table) are acceptable if the size and position are consistent with the inferred type.

if a furniture item is explicitly labele.rule: If a furniture item is explicitly labeled in the drawing but cannot be placed within 1 m of the label due to space constraints, the model should still include the item at the nearest valid location, and the discrepancy should be noted in the report.

an outer-wall opening whose approach is.rule: An outer-wall opening whose approach is blocked by a drawn piece and that has no outside destination is a window, not a door: read it at the floor's window sill.

a hall of about 2 m2 is a circulation no.rule: A hall of about 2 m2 is a circulation node, not a furnished room: it needs no furniture and no group.

a drawn piece that overlaps a drawn fixt.rule: A drawn piece that overlaps a drawn fixture in a wet room is moved to the nearest free spot clear of the fixture, not left overlapping.

a drawn piece that stands in front of a.rule: A drawn piece that stands in front of a window and blocks its light is moved to the nearest free spot clear of the opening.

a labelled site area (veranda, balcony,.rule: A labelled site area (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a distinct structure (slab, columns, roof) in the model, not left as an open slab or ignored.

a kitchen must be furnished with its cor.rule: A kitchen must be furnished with its core functional pieces (counters, sink, stove, fridge) visible in the scene; a kitchen with bare counters and no appliances is a failed build.

a living room with a dining area must ha.rule: A living room with a dining area must have its dining set (table and chairs) visible in the scene; a missing dining set is a failed build.

a children's room must be furnished appr.rule: A children's room must be furnished appropriately for its type (e.g., single bed or bunk bed, not two double beds); a room furnished like a guest room is a failed build.

a dressing room must be furnished with i.rule: A dressing room must be furnished with its core pieces (wardrobe, shoe cabinet) visible in the scene; a missing shoe cabinet is a failed build.

a bathroom with a washing machine must h.rule: A bathroom with a washing machine must have it visible in the scene; a missing washing machine is a failed build.

a bathroom must be furnished with its co.rule: A bathroom must be furnished with its core pieces (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) visible in the scene; a missing bathtub or a washbasin at an incorrect height is a failed build.
A bathroom must be furnished with its core pieces (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) visible in the scene; a missing bathtub or a floating washbasin is a failed build.

a hall must be furnished with its core p.rule: A hall must be furnished with its core pieces (shoe cabinet) visible in the scene; a missing shoe cabinet is a failed build.

a bedroom must be furnished with its cor.rule: A bedroom must be furnished with its core piece (bed) visible in the scene; a missing bed is a failed build.

a living room must be furnished with its.rule: A living room must be furnished with its core piece (sofa) visible in the scene; a missing sofa is a failed build.

a labelled veranda or covered terrace in.rule: A labelled veranda or covered terrace in the site plan must be built as a distinct structural element (slab, columns, roof) and not left as an open gap or ignored.

a labelled balcony in the site plan must.rule: A labelled balcony in the site plan must be built as a distinct structural element (slab, railing) and not left as an open area or ignored.

a named piece of furniture in the docume.rule: A named piece of furniture in the documents must be built in the model, even if it is not explicitly drawn.

a dressing room must have a mirror, a be.rule: A dressing room must have a mirror, a bench, or a vanity table in addition to a wardrobe.

a hall or entrance must have a shoe cabi.rule: A hall or entrance must have a shoe cabinet or a similar storage piece.

a bathroom or shower room must have a wa.rule: A bathroom or shower room must have a washing machine if it is listed in the JSON.

a kitchen must have a stove and a fridge.rule: A kitchen must have a stove and a fridge if they are listed in the JSON.

a living room or salon must have a dinin.rule: A living room or salon must have a dining table and chairs if they are listed in the JSON.

a room's main piece (the bed in a bedroo.rule: A room's main piece (the bed in a bedroom) must be built and visible in the render; if the build stage drops it, the stage must re-run until the piece is present.

a site area labeled in the documents (e..rule: A site area labeled in the documents (e.g. VERANDA, BALKON) must be built with an outline and structure in the model; if the site stage leaves it as an open slab, the stage must re-run until the structure is present.

a room typed as a children's room must b.rule: A room typed as a children's room must be furnished with child-appropriate anchors (single or bunk beds, play area) rather than adult double beds; the furniture agent must respect the room's intended occupant profile when selecting bed types.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) must con.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) must contain a dressing table or vanity as its primary anchor piece, not just a shoe cabinet; the furniture agent must recognize 'dressing room' as requiring a vanity/dressing table group, distinct from a simple storage or hall room.

a bathroom or shower room that includes.rule: A bathroom or shower room that includes a washing machine in its piece list must have a valid placement strategy for the appliance; if the room is too small for a standard wc_set group, the washing machine should be placed as a standalone appliance or the room type should be adjusted to allow appliance placement without requiring a full wc_set group.

bathroom fixtures (bathtub, washbasin) m.rule: Bathroom fixtures (bathtub, washbasin) must be placed at their correct working heights and visible in the render; the fit stage must verify that all listed bathroom pieces are built and positioned correctly, not just listed.

hall rooms must have their main anchor p.rule: Hall rooms must have their main anchor piece (e.g., shoe cabinet) visible in the render; the fit stage must ensure that all listed hall pieces are built and positioned correctly, not just listed.

bedroom rooms must have their main ancho.rule: Bedroom rooms must have their main anchor piece (e.g., bed) visible in the render; the fit stage must ensure that all listed bedroom pieces are built and positioned correctly, not just listed.

small utility or hall rooms must have th.rule: Small utility or hall rooms must have their main anchor piece (e.g., shoe cabinet) visible in the render; the fit stage must ensure that all listed pieces are built and positioned correctly, not just listed.

bathroom fixtures must use library model.rule: Bathroom fixtures must use library models that are visible and correctly sized; if a fixture is missing from the render, swap to a model that is known to render correctly.

kitchen appliances must use library mode.rule: Kitchen appliances must use library models that are visible and correctly sized; if an appliance is missing from the render, swap to a model that is known to render correctly.

dining tables must use library models th.rule: Dining tables must use library models that are visible and correctly sized; if a table is missing from the render, swap to a model that is known to render correctly.

appliances must use library models that.rule: Appliances must use library models that are visible and correctly sized; if an appliance is missing from the render, swap to a model that is known to render correctly.

desks in children's rooms should use mod.rule: Desks in children's rooms should use models that are appropriate for the room's function; if a desk is missing from the render, swap to a model that is known to render correctly.

shoe cabinets must use library models th.rule: Shoe cabinets must use library models that are visible and correctly sized; if a shoe cabinet is missing from the render, swap to a model that is known to render correctly.

a piece placed by the fit stage must not.rule: A piece placed by the fit stage must not stand in the approach of a window or door on the same wall; the fit stage must clear the opening's sightline before it reports the room as fitted.

a 2.15 m opening in an outer wall with n.rule: A 2.15 m opening in an outer wall with no swing arc and no outside landing (furniture across its approach) is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

a gap in an outer wall of a wet room wit.rule: A gap in an outer wall of a wet room with furniture across its approach and no outside landing is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

a gap in an outer wall with the kitchen.rule: A gap in an outer wall with the kitchen counter across its approach and no outside landing is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

a gap in an outer wall with furniture ac.rule: A gap in an outer wall with furniture across its full width and no outside landing is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.
A gap in an outer wall with furniture across its approach and no outside landing is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

a 2.15 m opening in an outer wall with n.rule: A 2.15 m opening in an outer wall with no swing arc and furniture across its approach is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

a 0.65 m opening in an outer wall with f.rule: A 0.65 m opening in an outer wall with furniture across its full width and no outside landing is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

a 1.55 m opening in an outer wall with n.rule: A 1.55 m opening in an outer wall with no swing arc and furniture across its approach is a window, not a door; the reading stage must classify it as a window at the floor's sill.

the fit stage must not leave two drawn p.rule: The fit stage must not leave two drawn pieces overlapping; when a drawn fixture (bathtub) is kept, the other drawn piece must be moved to a free place in the room.

the big loop must run at least one full.rule: The big loop must run at least one full cycle before it stops; a stop with 0 cycles and no deadline means the loop did not do its job.

an interior camera marked for review mus.rule: An interior camera marked for review must be re-posed to show the room's main furniture set, not a bare wall or a single fixture.

when a tall storage piece (wardrobe, tal.rule: When a tall storage piece (wardrobe, tall cabinet) in a small room blocks an opening and no free wall span exists within the move tolerance, the solver must swap to a narrower model that fits the clear span, not attempt to move the piece to a non-existent free place.

when a low storage piece (dresser, sideb.rule: When a low storage piece (dresser, sideboard) in a bedroom stands in front of a window and blocks the sill, and no free wall span exists within the move tolerance, the solver must swap to a model that clears the window sill height, or the architect must raise the window sill.

when a kitchen room's kitchen_run group.rule: When a kitchen room's kitchen_run group is missing key fixtures (fridge, stove, sink), the solver must complete the group with the missing pieces, not attempt to relayout the room.

when a bed in a bedroom with a sloped ce.rule: When a bed in a bedroom with a sloped ceiling has its headboard not against a wall and no free wall span exists within the move tolerance, the solver must swap to a lower-profile bed model that fits under the sloped ceiling, or the architect must adjust the ceiling height.

when a washing machine in a bathroom is.rule: When a washing machine in a bathroom is rendered as a flat panel (not a recognizable appliance), the solver must swap to a proper washing machine model with a visible door and controls, not a generated model with guessed units.

when a storage room (soyunma odası) is b.rule: When a storage room (soyunma odası) is bare and empty, the solver must place a dressing group in it, including a mirror, a hanging rail, and a garment on a hook, to match the reference.

an exterior view of a large window that.rule: An exterior view of a large window that opens onto a flat, empty green field must have a believable outdoor scene with depth, planters, or detail, not a void.

a terrace and the base of a facade that.rule: A terrace and the base of a facade that are bare concrete and wood with no planters or greenery must have planters or greenery to soften the transition to the lawn.

a camera view of a children's room that.rule: A camera view of a children's room that shows a generic, empty master bedroom must be re-posed to show the room's main pieces (wardrobe, desk, office chair) and styling layers (rug, wall art).

when a children's room has a bare wood f.rule: When a children's room has a bare wood floor, the solver must place a rug to define the sleeping or play zone, matching the reference.

when a dresser in a children's room has.rule: When a dresser in a children's room has a completely empty top, the solver must place decorative objects (lamps, frames, plants) on it to match the reference.

when a children's room has a bare wood f.rule: When a children's room has a bare wood floor, the solver must place a soft, colorful rug to define the play/sleep zone and match the reference's warmth.

a bathroom camera view that shows a bare.rule: A bathroom camera view that shows a bare, unstyled shell must be re-posed to show the room's main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) and styling layers (towel warmer, mirror).

when a bathroom lacks warm light, the so.rule: When a bathroom lacks warm light, the solver must add a warm light source (e.g., a warm-toned ceiling light or a wall sconce) to match the reference.

a bathroom camera view that shows a bare.rule: A bathroom camera view that shows a bare, unstyled shell with a missing washbasin must be re-posed to show the room's main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) and styling layers.

a room typed as a child's room must be f.rule: A room typed as a child's room must be furnished with a child-appropriate set (scaled bed, playful palette, age-appropriate decor); a generic adult bedroom set is a mismatch of the room's program.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main functional group, not a corner or a single fixture; a close-up of a partition is not a room presentation.

a bad camera is fixed by re-aiming the c.rule: A bad camera is fixed by re-aiming the camera, not by moving the furniture to fit the camera.

a bathroom must be styled with warm mate.rule: A bathroom must be styled with warm materials, texture, and lived-in details (mirrors, wood, plants, lighting); a flat untextured 'grey box' is not client-ready.

a shower enclosure model must be a clean.rule: A shower enclosure model must be a clean, stylish glass partition, not a visual mess of vertical bars and reflections that looks like a construction error.

chairs in a room must form a cohesive se.rule: Chairs in a room must form a cohesive set matching the room's aesthetic; three different styles clashing with the bed and reference is a mismatched set.

a floor lamp must match the room's warm,.rule: A floor lamp must match the room's warm, paper-lantern style; a generic modern tripod does not provide the soft, warm ambient lighting the reference establishes.

windows in a bedroom must be softened wi.rule: Windows in a bedroom must be softened with fabric (curtains) to match the reference's warm, layered aesthetic; bare glass is a missing layer.

a hall must be styled with functional fu.rule: A hall must be styled with functional furniture (shoe cabinet, bench, hooks), wall art, lighting, and warm materials; a bare, unfinished landing is not client-ready.

a hall must contain the functional furni.rule: A hall must contain the functional furniture shown in the reference (shoe cabinet, bench, hooks); an empty hall is a missing layer.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group, not a corner and a door; a close-up of a wall corner is not a room presentation.

a bad camera is fixed by re-aiming the c.rule: A bad camera is fixed by re-aiming the camera, not by changing the room type.

walls in a bedroom must have decorative.rule: Walls in a bedroom must have decorative elements (wall art) to match the reference's warm, layered aesthetic; completely bare walls are a missing layer.

a bedroom must be styled with soft furni.rule: A bedroom must be styled with soft furnishings, decor, and texture to match the reference's warm, organic, and layered standard; a stark, unfinished 'grey box' is not client-ready.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's space and its contents, not be pressed against a piece of furniture; a view that is 80% white paneling and a door leaf is not a room presentation.

an interior camera of a small room (unde.rule: An interior camera of a small room (under 8 m2) must frame the room's main furniture and at least one wall, never a bare wall or a door; if no free point shows the furniture, the view is removed, not kept.

a covered outdoor space (veranda, terrac.rule: A covered outdoor space (veranda, terrace, balcony) larger than 4 m2 must carry at least one seating group (table and chairs) so it reads as usable, not an empty shell.

exterior renders must carry a sun (azimu.rule: Exterior renders must carry a sun (azimuth and elevation), a ground material and at least a few trees or a hedge; a flat overcast void with lollipop trees is a grey-box, not a presentation.

exterior and window views must carry a s.rule: Exterior and window views must carry a sun so that windows show interior light or reflection; dark, flat windows read as an unfinished shell.

a decor item that cannot rest on its hos.rule: A decor item that cannot rest on its host (penetration or gap beyond tolerance) is dropped, not forced; the host furniture is still built and the room is not incomplete.

a drawn piece whose footprint is 60% or.rule: A drawn piece whose footprint is 60% or more inside another piece's footprint is a detail of that piece (a sink bowl, an appliance front, a lamp base) and is not a piece of its own; the AI naming of such a detail must not override the containment rule.

the reading stage must read attdef entit.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF entities (attribute definitions) in DWG files; they often carry room labels, dimensions or furniture tags that the ledger checks.

site decor read on a level other than th.rule: Site decor read on a level other than the ground floor (L0) is not used for the site (the site is the ground floor's); the reading must tag site items with their level and the site stage must only use L0 items.

when a room outline holds two labels (e..rule: When a room outline holds two labels (e.g. 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ'), the reading must check whether a wall separates the two labelled areas; if not, the second label is a sub-zone of the first room, not a room of its own, and the room's area is the sum of both.

every printed area label in the document.rule: Every printed area label in the documents must be matched to a room in the model; if the label's area does not match any room's area, the reading must flag it for review rather than silently dropping it.

when the wall-layer evidence already clo.rule: When the wall-layer evidence already closes the labelled rooms, off-layer wall primitives on the runner-up layer are duplicates, not lost walls; do not flag them as a loss.

decor symbols read outside the upper flo.rule: Decor symbols read outside the upper floor's walls that repeat the ground plan's symbols at the same place are the ground floor's site, not lost items of the upper floor.

furniture layers (bathtub, sink, etc.) w.rule: Furniture layers (bathtub, sink, etc.) whose item is already built in the model are not lost building elements; do not flag their raw line entities as unused.

when one room outline holds two labels a.rule: When one room outline holds two labels and the second is a sub-zone (dining, antre) with no separating wall, the reading must keep the larger label and record the sub-zone as a zone of the room, not as a lost room; the building stage must not expect a separate room for it.

when a drawn piece is a few centimetres.rule: When a drawn piece is a few centimetres off its drawn place and the current model's footprint prevents a tighter fit, swap to a model whose footprint matches the drawn size so the fit solver can re-seat it.

when a drawn dresser (or similar low sto.rule: When a drawn dresser (or similar low storage) is placed in front of a window and no other free wall span exists within 1.2 m of its drawn centre, the layout stage must accept the drawn position and the check must raise the tolerance for pieces drawn in front of windows, or the architect must move the window.

when a drawn wardrobe is placed in front.rule: When a drawn wardrobe is placed in front of a window and no other free wall span exists, the layout stage must accept the drawn position and the check must raise the tolerance for pieces drawn in front of windows, or the architect must move the window.

when an elevation has no north arrow or.rule: When an elevation has no north arrow or view bearing, the reading stage must record the elevation's side from the plan's axis grid or section marks, or the check must skip the elevation-to-plan comparison and flag it as 'not checkable' rather than 'could not run'.

when a drawn section's ends do not align.rule: When a drawn section's ends do not align with the plan's roof outline (over 0.30 m apart), the check must skip the point-by-point comparison and flag the section as 'not aligned with plan' rather than 'could not run'.
when a drawn section's ends do not align.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

when a shoe_cabinet (or similar entrance.rule: When a shoe_cabinet (or similar entrance furniture) in a hall blocks a door and no free position exists that clears the door swing and other fixed elements, the agent must remove the piece (it is not essential) rather than retrying moves, and the layout stage must not place entrance furniture in a door swing.

when no library model of the building's.rule: When no library model of the building's window family fits the opening's size, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct fallback; do not flag it as a missing model.

when no library model of a window family.rule: When no library model of a window family fits the drawn size, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct build, not a defect.

when a fitting is built below the librar.rule: When a fitting is built below the library level, swap to a library model that fits the piece's size and the room's style.

when no library model of a wall_cabinet.rule: When no library model of a wall_cabinet fits the drawn size, the parametric mesh is the correct build; the library should be expanded to include more wall_cabinet sizes.

when a washbasin looks unstyled and clas.rule: When a washbasin looks unstyled and clashes with the room's aesthetic, swap to a library model that matches the style and fits the size.

when kitchen cabinetry looks like a plai.rule: When kitchen cabinetry looks like a plain, flat white placeholder, set the material to a warm wood tone that matches the reference.

when a fridge looks like a generic, indu.rule: When a fridge looks like a generic, industrial placeholder, swap to a library model that matches the room's warm, wood-and-white aesthetic.

when a coffee table looks like a generic.rule: When a coffee table looks like a generic, low-poly placeholder, swap to a library model with more detail and material richness.

curtains and other soft window treatment.rule: Curtains and other soft window treatments are not part of the furniture library; the pipeline should either add them to the library or the finding should be marked as out of scope.

when a bedroom lacks bedside lighting, a.rule: When a bedroom lacks bedside lighting, add the missing functional group (e.g. sleeping_single) that includes a nightstand and lamp.

when a washbasin looks unstyled with exp.rule: When a washbasin looks unstyled with exposed plumbing, swap to a library model with an integrated look.

cushions, throws, and other soft bedding.rule: Cushions, throws, and other soft bedding layers are not part of the furniture library; the pipeline should either add them to the library or the finding should be marked as out of scope.

styled surfaces (books, small decor) are.rule: Styled surfaces (books, small decor) are not part of the furniture library; the pipeline should either add them to the library or the finding should be marked as out of scope.

when a stair railing looks like a generi.rule: When a stair railing looks like a generic, industrial placeholder, set the material to a warm wood tone that matches the project's style.

bed models in the library must include b.rule: Bed models in the library must include bedding (mattress, pillows, duvet) and a throw as part of the asset; a bare frame is not an acceptable bed model for any style.

windows in living and bedroom rooms must.rule: Windows in living and bedroom rooms must be furnished with curtains or blinds as part of the room's decor set; bare windows are not acceptable for a furnished render.

interior doors must use a styled model (.rule: Interior doors must use a styled model (panelled, flush with hardware detail) matching the project's style; a plain flat slab is not acceptable for a furnished render.

when a piece is removed by an explicit a.rule: When a piece is removed by an explicit AI.remove_piece action, the build stage must not flag its absence as a conservation loss; the removal is a valid design decision.

drawn clusters exceeding 4.5 m in length.rule: Drawn clusters exceeding 4.5 m in length that do not match standard furniture dimensions should be treated as architectural built-ins or wall units, not as individual furniture pieces, and excluded from the parametric furniture build.

drawn marks thinner than 0.2 m that do n.rule: Drawn marks thinner than 0.2 m that do not fit any furniture type should be treated as architectural details (e.g., taps, valves, thresholds) and not built as furniture.

drawn marks that are 60% or more contain.rule: Drawn marks that are 60% or more contained within another piece of furniture should be treated as details of that piece (e.g., pillows, blankets) and not built as separate furniture.

when a nightstand cannot be placed witho.rule: When a nightstand cannot be placed without cutting the bed, the build stage should attempt to swap to a smaller or differently shaped nightstand model before marking it as not built.

when a shoe_cabinet cannot be placed wit.rule: When a shoe_cabinet cannot be placed without blocking a door, the build stage should attempt to swap to a smaller or differently shaped shoe_cabinet model before marking it as not built.

the upper end of a stair that leads to t.rule: The upper end of a stair that leads to the top floor should not be built again as a separate piece; it is already represented by the stair on the lower floor.

decorative elements that depend on a hos.rule: Decorative elements that depend on a host piece should not be flagged as lost if the host piece is being addressed by a fix; they will be built once the host is built.
Decorative elements that depend on a host piece that was intentionally removed should not be flagged as lost; they are correctly not built.

when a site area (veranda, balcony, terr.rule: When a site area (veranda, balcony, terrace) is identified in the drawing with a label and outline, the build stage must construct its floor slab, edge, and any drawn steps or guard rails as part of the site model, even if the area is not a room.

when a room contains a labeled sub-zone.rule: When a room contains a labeled sub-zone (e.g., 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ' for dining) that is large enough to be a functional area, the reading stage should either split the room into two rooms (living + dining) or type the room as 'living' with a dining group placed within it, ensuring the dining table and chairs are in the same room as the dining zone label.

a piece whose type was inferred from con.rule: A piece whose type was inferred from context and is already built and consistent with its neighbours is not a defect; the inference log is informational.

when a drawn furniture label is present.rule: When a drawn furniture label is present but the solver cannot place the piece within 1 m of the label due to room congestion, the system should either (a) relax the placement tolerance to 2 m for storage pieces in bedrooms, or (b) automatically trigger a relayout of the room to free up space near the label before attempting placement.

an outer opening that is blocked by furn.rule: An outer opening that is blocked by furniture such that it cannot function as a passage should be reclassified as a window if its dimensions and position are consistent with a window (e.g., sill height, width) and there is no other door providing access to that part of the facade.

a room with an area less than 3 m2 and t.rule: A room with an area less than 3 m2 and type 'hall' or 'stair' is not expected to contain furniture; the absence of furniture is not a defect.

furniture that blocks a window or door o.rule: Furniture that blocks a window or door opening must be moved to a free position in the room that does not obstruct the opening.

a labelled outdoor extension (veranda, t.rule: A labelled outdoor extension (veranda, terrace, balcony) in the documents must be built as a platform with its own floor, roof, and glazing, not ignored.

a room under 3 m2 with no fixtures is a.rule: A room under 3 m2 with no fixtures is a hall or storage, not a room.

a kitchen must have a functional run wit.rule: A kitchen must have a functional run with a sink, hob, and fridge, not just bare counters.

a living room with a dining area must ha.rule: A living room with a dining area must have a dining table and chairs.

a children's room should have age-approp.rule: A children's room should have age-appropriate furniture, such as a bunk bed or single beds, not adult double beds.

site areas labelled in the plan (veranda.rule: Site areas labelled in the plan (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be built as floor slabs with railings or glazing, not skipped when they lack a closed wall outline.

a room typed as a children's bedroom mus.rule: A room typed as a children's bedroom must be furnished with child-appropriate furniture (bunk beds, cribs, single beds), not standard double beds.

a kitchen room must have a complete func.rule: A kitchen room must have a complete functional run including a sink, hob/stove, and counter space, not just bare counter boxes.

a living room (salon) that is programmed.rule: A living room (salon) that is programmed to include a dining area must have a dining table and chairs placed in it.

a bathroom room must have its main fixtu.rule: A bathroom room must have its main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) placed and visible, not just listed in the room's pieces.

a hall or entrance room must have its ma.rule: A hall or entrance room must have its main functional piece (e.g., shoe cabinet, console table) placed and visible.

furniture strokes on the 'tefriş' layer.rule: Furniture strokes on the 'tefriş' layer that form recognizable sets (e.g., sofa with chairs) must be read as individual pieces even if they are not explicitly labeled, to prevent loss of drawn furniture.

the main functional piece of a room (e.g.rule: The main functional piece of a room (e.g., bed in a bedroom) must always be built and visible; if it is listed in the room's pieces but not visible in the render, the build stage must be rerun or the piece re-placed.

site areas labeled in the documents (e.g.rule: Site areas labeled in the documents (e.g., VERANDA, BALKON) must be built with outlines and structures if they are part of the building's program, not just open slabs.

a storage room whose program is a dressi.rule: A storage room whose program is a dressing set must have its wardrobe placed by the fitting stage; when the solver reports no place, the stage must retry with the room's free spans before the piece is left unbuilt.

a bathroom or wc room that lists a washi.rule: A bathroom or WC room that lists a washing machine must have it placed by the fitting stage; the group solver must not reject the room type when the piece is explicitly in the room's program.

a bathroom's main fixtures (bathtub, toi.rule: A bathroom's main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) must all be placed and visible; the fitting stage must verify that each listed piece is built and at its correct working height before the room is marked complete.

a hall's main piece (shoe cabinet) must.rule: A hall's main piece (shoe cabinet) must be placed by the fitting stage; when a relayout is refused due to walkway constraints, the fit stage must find an alternative position that satisfies both the piece placement and the circulation requirement.
A hall's main piece (shoe cabinet) must be placed by the fitting stage; the room type is already correct, so the issue is purely a placement failure.

a bedroom's main piece (bed) must be pla.rule: A bedroom's main piece (bed) must be placed by the fitting stage; the room is 11.3 m2 and the bed_single is listed, so the fit stage must place it.

a small hall or entry room's main piece.rule: A small hall or entry room's main piece (shoe cabinet) must be placed by the fitting stage; the room type attempts were no-ops, so the issue is purely a placement failure.

a bathroom render must show all three ma.rule: A bathroom render must show all three main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin); the camera must be positioned to include all of them in frame.

a dining table in a kitchen must use a m.rule: A dining table in a kitchen must use a model that matches the project's style chain (scandinavian -> minimal -> modern) and fits the room's dimensions; the current model is industrial style and not built.

a washing machine must use a real produc.rule: A washing machine must use a real product model that fits within the room's dimensions and matches the project's style; generated models with guessed units are not acceptable.

a bathroom or wc render must show all ma.rule: A bathroom or WC render must show all main fixtures; the camera must be positioned to include the washbasin, toilet, and shower in frame.

a hall render must show its main piece (.rule: A hall render must show its main piece (shoe cabinet); the camera must be positioned to include the shoe cabinet in frame.

a window opening must not be blocked by.rule: A window opening must not be blocked by furniture; the build stage must verify that no piece obstructs the ray through any opening.

an opening in the outer wall that is blo.rule: An opening in the outer wall that is blocked by furniture and has no passage function should be read as a window, not a door; the reading stage must check for furniture blocking the approach.

a warning that an opening is 'no passage.rule: A warning that an opening is 'no passage, read as a window' is a false alarm when the project facts already list that opening id under the floor's windows: the reading correction is applied and the warning is stale.

when a drawn fixture clashes with anothe.rule: When a drawn fixture clashes with another drawn piece in a wet room, the drawn fixture is kept and the other piece is moved to a free place in the room.

a piece that stands across the approach.rule: A piece that stands across the approach of a window and covers the opening is moved clear of the window.

when the big loop stops with no gain aft.rule: When the big loop stops with no gain after a single cycle, rerun the stage to allow more cycles to raise the house score.

a view marked for review is moved to a f.rule: A view marked for review is moved to a free point that shows the room's key pieces.

when a wardrobe in a small storage room.rule: When a wardrobe in a small storage room blocks a window and no free place on the wall clears it, the wardrobe is removed from the room (it does not belong there) and the room is re-typed or the window is re-read.

when a dresser's back is not on a wall a.rule: When a dresser's back is not on a wall and no free place on the wall is within 1.2 m of the drawn place, the dresser is moved to the nearest free place in the room, clear of the doorway or window.

a kitchen run group is not complete unti.rule: A kitchen run group is not complete until its required appliances (fridge, stove/hob, sink) are present and fitted; the group check must fail the layout (and block relayout) until the missing appliance is placed, so the agent is forced to add the missing piece rather than re-arranging the bare counter.

a dining area (table with chairs) in a k.rule: A dining area (table with chairs) in a kitchen or living room must be grounded by a rug; the furniture agent adds one when the reference shows a patterned area rug.

kitchen counters must use models that ma.rule: Kitchen counters must use models that match the project's material palette (e.g., wood fronts, stone tops) rather than generic parametric boxes.

appliances must use models that match th.rule: Appliances must use models that match the project's finish (matte, natural) rather than high-gloss generic assets.

kitchen renders must show a fully styled.rule: Kitchen renders must show a fully styled space with warm lighting, decor, and a complete dining set, not a bare shell.

kitchen renders must show all functional.rule: Kitchen renders must show all functional elements (wall cabinets, dining set) and decor to match the reference style.

living room furniture must form a cohere.rule: Living room furniture must form a coherent set with a unified style, and the room must be styled with soft layers (rugs, cushions) to match the reference.

sofas in a living room must match the st.rule: Sofas in a living room must match the style of the other main seating pieces to form a coherent set.

living rooms must be styled with soft te.rule: Living rooms must be styled with soft textiles (cushions, throws) on seating to match the reference's warm, layered look.

living room renders must show a coherent.rule: Living room renders must show a coherent, styled space with unified furniture and soft furnishings, not a bare shell.

living room renders must show a 'lived-i.rule: Living room renders must show a 'lived-in' space with rugs, art, and soft furnishings to match the reference.

dining areas must be grounded by a rug t.rule: Dining areas must be grounded by a rug to define the space and match the reference style.

armchairs in a living room must match th.rule: Armchairs in a living room must match the style of the other main seating pieces to form a coherent set.

bathroom renders must show a styled spac.rule: Bathroom renders must show a styled space with soft furnishings and all required fixtures (including the washing machine) to match the reference.

bathroom lighting must be warm and invit.rule: Bathroom lighting must be warm and inviting, not flat and clinical, to match the reference style.

child's rooms must be styled with playfu.rule: Child's rooms must be styled with playful, warm, and functional elements to match the reference, not as a generic master bedroom.

a room's furniture set must match its na.rule: A room's furniture set must match its named function and age group; a children's room must not be furnished as a generic adult master bedroom.

a single children's room should not cont.rule: A single children's room should not contain two double beds; the furniture set must be appropriate for the room's size and function.

room styling must reflect the room's spe.rule: Room styling must reflect the room's specific function and user demographic; a children's room requires playful and warm decor.

interior cameras must frame the main fun.rule: Interior cameras must frame the main functional pieces of the room, not just corners or secondary fixtures.

bathroom styling should include a mix of.rule: Bathroom styling should include a mix of textures (e.g., wood, stone) to avoid a sterile, flat appearance.

bathrooms must include functional detail.rule: Bathrooms must include functional details (mirrors, towel storage) and styling to feel like a designed space.

bedrooms should include plants (hanging.rule: Bedrooms should include plants (hanging or potted) to add warmth and life to the space.

furniture models must match the room's o.rule: Furniture models must match the room's overall style; a mid-century armchair clashes with a Scandinavian bedroom.

halls should include functional and styl.rule: Halls should include functional and stylistic elements (shoe cabinet, wall art, lighting, rug) to feel like a designed space.

halls should include a shoe cabinet and.rule: Halls should include a shoe cabinet and bench to address their main function as an entryway.

interior cameras must frame the room and.rule: Interior cameras must frame the room and its main furniture, not just corners or doors.

bedrooms should include wall art to add.rule: Bedrooms should include wall art to add visual interest and avoid bare walls.

bedrooms should include soft furnishings.rule: Bedrooms should include soft furnishings and decor to feel warm and lived-in.

an interior camera of a small storage or.rule: An interior camera of a small storage or hall room must frame the room's main furniture group, not a door leaf or a bare wall corner.

the exterior site must include a path an.rule: The exterior site must include a path and a front court (planting/hardscape) to soften the transition from the facade to the ground.

exterior renders must include warm inter.rule: Exterior renders must include warm interior light (windows glowing) and exterior fixtures so the house does not read as an unlit shell.

a decor item that cannot rest on its hos.rule: A decor item that cannot rest on its host without penetration is correctly not built; the host model's surface is the cause.
A decor item that cannot rest on its host without sufficient support is correctly not built; the host model's surface is the cause.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece's footprint is treated as a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own, even if an AI pass names it a separate type.

the reading stage must read attdef entit.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF entities in DWG files to capture block attribute definitions that may hold room labels or dimensions.

site decor read on upper levels (l1+) th.rule: Site decor read on upper levels (L1+) that repeats ground plan symbols at the same place is not used, as the site belongs to the ground floor (L0).

a shoe_cabinet in a hall must be placed.rule: A shoe_cabinet in a hall must be placed on a wall span that is not the swing or clearance zone of any door in that hall; if no such span exists, the piece is not built rather than blocking a door.

wall cabinets in a kitchen must be built.rule: Wall cabinets in a kitchen must be built with a library model if one is available; if no library model fits, the parametric mesh is acceptable but should be flagged for review.

windows in bedrooms and living areas sho.rule: Windows in bedrooms and living areas should have curtains or blinds added as a decor layer to match the reference style.

plants in the foreground of a render sho.rule: Plants in the foreground of a render should be chosen to match the organic, trailing style of the reference, avoiding stiff, uniform 'lollipop' looks.

interior doors should have some detail o.rule: Interior doors should have some detail or contrast (e.g., panels, handles, or a different finish) to avoid looking like flat, unadorned slabs.

nightstands and other small surfaces sho.rule: Nightstands and other small surfaces should have styled decor (e.g., books, small objects) to make the space feel personal and curated.

window and door surrounds must be given.rule: Window and door surrounds must be given a finished frame material (wood or painted) matching the project's style, never left as a plain white parametric box.

the approach path and door landing must.rule: The approach path and door landing must be given a defined paving material (a landing or material change at the door), not a single bare slab.

exterior renders must use a warm, believ.rule: Exterior renders must use a warm, believable sun (not a flat grey overcast void) so the home reads as a styled, lit residence.

an opening read twice (the same opening.rule: An opening read twice (the same opening detected on two passes) is built once; the duplicate read is not a loss.

structural grid bubbles (axis labels) an.rule: Structural grid bubbles (axis labels) and drawing annotations are not built; they are drawing marks, not house elements.

a cushion, pillow or detail drawn on a p.rule: A cushion, pillow or detail drawn on a piece is part of that piece, not a piece of its own; it is not built separately.

a column drawn on 'kolon' that is a post.rule: A column drawn on 'KOLON' that is a post of a veranda is built as part of that veranda structure, not as a separate lost element.

level mark symbols (kot) are drawing ann.rule: Level mark symbols (kot) are drawing annotations, not built elements.

an exterior label whose surface is built.rule: An exterior label whose surface is built from site paving/parking/grass is not a lost element; the surface is built as site ground.

one object read twice (two outlines of t.rule: One object read twice (two outlines of the same kitchen counter) is built once; the duplicate is not a loss.

a piece drawn inside another piece (60%.rule: A piece drawn inside another piece (60% or more) is the same piece drawn twice or a part of it; it is not built separately.

a kitchen run drawn as one outline with.rule: A kitchen run drawn as one outline with its fixtures is replaced by its counter legs along the walls; the run is built as its parts, not as one outline.

an outline around other pieces (a rug or.rule: An outline around other pieces (a rug or zone outline) is not a piece; rugs are laid under the groups by the decor rules.

a dining table whose model is not in the.rule: A dining table whose model is not in the project's style chain must be swapped to a model that is in the chain (scandinavian/minimal/modern) and fits the piece's size.

a 'not built' finding whose reason is 't.rule: A 'not built' finding whose reason is 'the answer to AI.remove_piece' is a false alarm: the removal was an intentional edit, not a stage dropping a drawn element.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is not a single furniture piece; it is either a wall, a built-in, or a misread. The build stage is correct to not build it as a single parametric piece.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m is a det.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m is a detail (tap, valve, threshold, shelf line), not a furniture piece. The build stage is correct to not build it as a piece.

a drawn mark that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn mark that is 60% or more inside another piece is a detail of that piece, not a separate piece. The build stage is correct to not build it as a separate item.

when a nightstand cannot be placed witho.rule: When a nightstand cannot be placed without cutting the bed and no free place is found within 1.0 m, the nightstand should be removed or the bed should be moved to make space, rather than leaving the nightstand unbuilt.

a stair that arrives from a lower level.rule: A stair that arrives from a lower level and has no level above is not built again on the upper level. This is correct behavior for a stair that terminates at the top floor.

when a host piece is not built due to a.rule: When a host piece is not built due to a spatial conflict, the decorations on it should also be removed or the host should be moved to make space, rather than leaving both unbuilt.

when a host piece is removed by an expli.rule: When a host piece is removed by an explicit action, the decorations on it should also be removed, rather than leaving them unbuilt.

a decorative element whose host piece is.rule: A decorative element whose host piece is not built is not a conservation loss; it is dropped with its host.

a door symbol on a symbol layer is a dra.rule: A door symbol on a symbol layer is a drawing annotation, not a built element; it is not a conservation loss.

a hatch on a hatching layer is a drawing.rule: A hatch on a hatching layer is a drawing annotation, not a built element; it is not a conservation loss.

an outdoor-space edge or step detail is.rule: An outdoor-space edge or step detail is built with its host outdoor space; it is not a separate conservation loss.

when the building frame is offset from t.rule: When the building frame is offset from the sheet outline corner, the reading must anchor the model to the sheet frame (or record the offset) so that all regions and coordinates are consistent with the sheet, not with an arbitrary corner.

when the section prints the ground floor.rule: When the section prints the ground floor at a non-zero level (e.g. +0.50), the reading must shift the plan level marks by that offset so that building z 0 matches the printed datum.

a small drawn piece around a level-mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level-mark text is a level-mark symbol, not furniture; it must be marked as such, not built.

a furniture name text that matches an al.rule: A furniture name text that matches an already-built piece in the room is not a loss; it is accounted for.

a furniture name text in a room that doe.rule: A furniture name text in a room that does not have that piece is a reading note; it is not a conservation loss unless the documents show the piece should be there.

a zone label within a room (e.g. 'yemek.rule: A zone label within a room (e.g. 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ' in a living room) is a sub-zone, not a separate room; the reading must not treat it as a second room label.

a piece typed by context (size, position.rule: A piece typed by context (size, position, orientation relative to a table) is a correct reading, not a loss.

a drawn furniture label whose nearest va.rule: A drawn furniture label whose nearest valid placement in its room is more than 1 m from the text is a misread or a label for a piece outside the room: do not add a piece at the text position, and flag the label for manual review instead of silently dropping it.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrac.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrace, balcony) that the plan outlines and the model partially builds must be registered as a site area with its own floor, railing and furniture set, not left as unbounded ad-hoc geometry.

a sub-3 m2 enclosed space with no fixtur.rule: A sub-3 m2 enclosed space with no fixtures and no door of its own is not a room; it must be re-typed as a hall/landing or merged into the adjacent room, never left as a doorless 'other' room.

a kitchen room must be built as a comple.rule: A kitchen room must be built as a complete, working run (counter + sink + hob + worktop) as one group; a kitchen whose counters are bare boxes with no sink or hob is a failed kitchen run, not a furnished kitchen.

a living room whose program includes a d.rule: A living room whose program includes a dining set must have that set placed as a coherent group (table + chairs) in the room; a dining table listed in the program but absent from the room is a lost dining group.

a bathroom room must be built as a compl.rule: A bathroom room must be built as a complete set (bathtub or shower + toilet + washbasin) as one group; a bathroom whose main fixture (bathtub/shower) is listed but absent is a failed bathroom set.

a children's room programmed for one chi.rule: A children's room programmed for one child must have exactly one bed; a second double bed in a single-child room is a misread or duplicate sleeping piece and must be re-typed to a single bed or removed.

a floor should have one main hall; a sec.rule: A floor should have one main hall; a second sub-4 m2 'hall' with a shoe cabinet is a misread entrance or landing and must be re-typed (storage, hall-landing) or merged into the main hall.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcon.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcony, terrace) that the plan outlines must be built as a platform with its own floor and glazing/railing; 'no outline' is a read failure, not a valid reason to drop it.

a small interior room (under ~5 m2) that.rule: A small interior room (under ~5 m2) that holds a shoe cabinet or wardrobe and has no entrance door is a storage/utility room, not a hall; retype it so its furniture and access make sense.

a room labelled dressing/soyunma must ca.rule: A room labelled dressing/soyunma must carry a dressing set (mirror, bench, chest) in addition to its wardrobe; a lone wardrobe is not a dressing room.

a shoe cabinet belongs at the entrance h.rule: A shoe cabinet belongs at the entrance hall of the ground floor, not in an upper-floor hall; an upper hall's storage anchor is a console or coat stand.

site areas labeled as 'veranda' or 'balk.rule: Site areas labeled as 'VERANDA' or 'BALKON' in the plan must be explicitly built as distinct site elements with their own geometry (deck, posts, roof) and linked to the corresponding interior doors, rather than being absorbed into the main building volume or ignored.

site areas defined in the plan (like bal.rule: Site areas defined in the plan (like balconies or verandas) must be built if they are indicated by railings or doors, even if the 'outline' flag is missing.

a level whose rooms survive into the fin.rule: A level whose rooms survive into the final stage must have its full wall set and door openings rebuilt by the build stage; if a level's walls are dropped, the build stage must be re-run to reconstruct them from the drawing rather than leaving the level's rooms open.

the build stage must cut every door, win.rule: The build stage must cut every door, window and opening the reading stage placed on a wall; an opening that exists in the reading but is absent from the built walls is a build failure, not a reading error.

every site area the documents label (par.rule: Every site area the documents label (parking, terrace, pool) must be built as a modelled outdoor space with its outline; a labelled site area left unbuilt with no reason is a site-stage loss.

every room the documents name with a lab.rule: Every room the documents name with a label and area must be created in the model; a named room with no matching model room is a reading-stage loss.

the build stage must not drop furniture.rule: The build stage must not drop furniture that the final stage places; every piece present in the final stage must be carried through the build stage.

the build stage must preserve every furn.rule: The build stage must preserve every furniture piece placed by the final stage; if a piece is missing after build, the build stage must be re-run to restore it.

pieces placed by the decor stage must be.rule: Pieces placed by the decor stage must be preserved by the build stage; if a piece is missing, the build stage must re-place it.

a dedicated stair room whose only camera.rule: A dedicated stair room whose only camera point is inside the stair core must be shown from the adjacent hall, not given its own interior view.

a drawn piece that is read as unknown mu.rule: A drawn piece that is read as unknown must be typed or marked with evidence before the run is accepted; it may not be left untyped and unbuilt without a record.

a drawn block that names a fixture (stov.rule: A drawn block that names a fixture (stove, toilet, etc.) must be added to the model as that fixture; a drawn fixture with no model element is a loss.

a drawn fixture block that falls inside.rule: A drawn fixture block that falls inside a room the model has already furnished with the same fixture type is a duplicate ledger entry, not a lost piece; the reading stage must match drawn blocks to already-built pieces by room and type before flagging them as lost.

a small wall cabinet drawn inside a bath.rule: A small wall cabinet drawn inside a bathroom that is already furnished as a complete wet set is an optional accessory; the ledger must not flag it as a lost major piece when the room's core fixtures are present.

in an open-plan room where the kitchen z.rule: In an open-plan room where the kitchen zone is already furnished, a drawn kitchen sink block that falls within that zone is a duplicate of the built sink, not a lost piece.

a drawn stove block inside a room that a.rule: A drawn stove block inside a room that already has a built stove is a duplicate ledger entry, not a lost piece.

a drawn toilet block inside a bathroom t.rule: A drawn toilet block inside a bathroom that already has a built toilet is a duplicate ledger entry, not a lost piece.

a drawn washbasin block inside a bathroo.rule: A drawn washbasin block inside a bathroom that already has a built washbasin is a duplicate ledger entry, not a lost piece.

a small wall cabinet drawn inside a full.rule: A small wall cabinet drawn inside a fully furnished bathroom is an optional accessory; the ledger must not flag it as a lost major piece.

a drawn kitchen sink block inside a room.rule: A drawn kitchen sink block inside a room that already has a built kitchen sink is a duplicate ledger entry, not a lost piece.

a stair layer whose geometry is consumed.rule: A stair layer whose geometry is consumed by a built stair piece must be linked to that piece in the ledger; an unlinked stair layer is a false 'lost' finding when the stair is already present in the model.

stair elevation layers are reference vie.rule: Stair elevation layers are reference views of an already-built stair; they must not be flagged as lost 3D elements.

a decorative sanitary-ware layer whose g.rule: A decorative sanitary-ware layer whose geometry corresponds to already-built bathroom fixtures must be linked to those pieces; it is not a separate lost element.

a sanitary-ware detail layer whose geome.rule: A sanitary-ware detail layer whose geometry corresponds to already-built fixtures must be linked to those pieces; it is not a separate lost element.

an opening whose door ray intersects its.rule: An opening whose door ray intersects its host wall is not properly cut; the build stage must re-cut the opening through the wall before the scene is accepted.

a kitchen counter's top must be at or ne.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at or near the standard working height (0.90–0.97 m); a counter top significantly above this height indicates a scaling or positioning error in the build stage.

the sheets stage must not end 'pending'.rule: The sheets stage must not end 'pending' with unresolved questions; the reading stage must resolve all sheet questions before the pipeline proceeds to the next stage.

a small drawn symbol that sits mostly in.rule: A small drawn symbol that sits mostly inside a larger drawn piece of the same type in the same room is a double-drawn symbol of that one piece, not a second piece; the reading must keep the larger one and drop the inner duplicate.

a drawn piece that an ai pass has named.rule: A drawn piece that an AI pass has named and whose size fits that name must be built as that named piece, even when it is drawn overlapping a larger piece; the overlap is a drawing offset, not a reason to drop it as a detail.

entities on layers that are off, frozen.rule: Entities on layers that are off, frozen or invisible in the source DWG are not part of the issued drawing and must not be read; the ledger must not flag them as lost.
entities on layers that are off, frozen.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

ole2frame and wipeout entities are annot.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are annotation/occlusion graphics, not building geometry or furniture, and must not be read as pieces; the ledger must not flag them as lost.

a camera view that exists in the baselin.rule: A camera view that exists in the baseline must not be dropped by a later stage without a recorded reason; if a view is removed, the stage must state why, and an exterior view of the building is never dropped silently.
